We especially loved the Chicken Curry, Sizzling Pork and the Salt And Vinegar Chicken. So in conclusion, don't be put off by the building, embrace its oddity and remember the only reason Knife and Fork hasn't had more reviews on here is because it hasn't been open for long. Would advise any future guests and travellers to avoid!What we ordered: 358 RM 9 course 'surprise' chefs tasting menu + non alcoholic drinks pairingService: Overall the servers were nice, but not very professional. They were also not introduced in detail by our server..Portion size: The portions were also very tight...my girlfriend wasn't even full after 9 courses. Some courses were embarrassingly small.Ambience & setting: The view off the external balcony is a slight redeeming feature of this venue. But there is overall a lack of attention to detail by the staff in the dining atmosphere. We heard utensils being washed behind the open bar, the reception mobile going off often & loudly. The bathroom was also unfit for a fine dining venue in terms of decor and the soap dispenser hadn't even been filled. The background music in the dining room was a loop of Christmas carols quite noisy, noticeable and maddening.

This old building houses the Farquhar Mansion Penang Fine Dining & Lounge which serves a mix of French & Contemporary cuisine. The dining areas on the ground floor have been decorated with plush colonial style furnishings like satin drapes and velvet chairs. The flooring retained the original sexe-en- trent colourful tiles.Located upstairs are more dining rooms with a banquet room. The decor here is contemporary and the ceiling has a collage of framed pictures, several of them op- art. I attended a birthday dinner in the banquet room on 27 April 2019 and enjoyed "The Ultimate Chef Tasting Menu" which consisted of French/Contemporary cuisine. The nouveau cuisine had contrasts in flavours, textures and tastes that challenge the taste buds. Food was artistically presented with designs and colours on plates like paintings. A lot of thought would have gone into the creation of each dish. The Maitre' d' explained what each dish consisted of when each course was served.Food was fresh and good. Food gourmets would be able to differentiate the subtle differences of the flavours of each dish and appreciate the creativity of the artistically presented food and the wafting flavours to encourage the tasting. For those expecting the traditional flavours of French cuisine be surprised by a few extra "punch" in these dishes.Highly recommended for those adventurous enough seeking something different and be prepared to pay for the experience.Service was good and staff were attentive.

Review: This was a wonderful place to discover. The Loft situated just off a busting road in Love Lane is one to visit if you need a break from the hustle and bustle of Penang. The modern urban decor with industrialist features will make you feel …MoreThis was a wonderful place to discover. The Loft situated just off a busting road in Love Lane is one to visit if you need a break from the hustle and bustle of Penang. The modern urban decor with industrialist features will make you feel instantly calm.The drinks - a wonderful selection of drinks was available, my partner and I tried a few cocktails and they were all delicious. The Long Island Iced Tea was quite strong so would be nice to see it made a bit more traditionally but the mojito was delicious.The food - The Italian inspired menu definitely has a great variety of options to choose from. The starters that my partner ordered (focaccia and dips & calamari) both were sensational. The focaccia bread is made in-house and tasted amazing, we just wished there was more of it to go with the dips provided. The 2 pizzas that we ordered were top notch, better than some of the pizzas I’ve had in my own country.The staff - All of the workers were super friendly and helpful. One staff member was confused by the cocktails we ordered so we though he might be new but another person helped him out. The staff did keep coming over to check how everything was perhaps a little too often, it was borderline annoying and interrupting when I was having a conversation with my partner. I did appreciate that they asked us for feedback on the pizza and if we thought there needed to be any improvement - no improvement needed for the pizzas though.The only other negative was that our food arrived all relatively quickly together, once our entree had arrived within about 5 minutes when we had just started them our mains (pizzas) arrived. Then once we finished our entrees and they cleared it away, the wait person shoved our pizzas in front us almost like thy were forcing us to eat it straight away. The was a little annoying as we would have liked some time between the courses to enjoy our drinks and not feel so rushed.Overall a really wonderful place and I’d recommend and visit again.

Review: Great cocktails, burgers, music and just feels like coming home!I first tripped over the lovely Junk almost exactly a year ago, fell in love …MoreGreat cocktails, burgers, music and just feels like coming home!I first tripped over the lovely Junk almost exactly a year ago, fell in love with the general welcoming vibe, tunes, food, cocktails...plus made a firm friend in top man, Prakash. So I knew it would be first on my list when I finally broke out of KL CMCO this Christmas.COVID has had an unfortunate effect on most of us, not least Junk, which has had to move (just a little bit!) round the corner, so if 401 Chulia Street is still showing as it is as I type this, do make sure you venture just a tiny bit further to 1, Jalan Pintal Tali. It's well worth it, I promise.For food - burgers are it. I don't eat meat (so the Grilled Vegetable or The Great White both more than float my boat) but if you do, you're in burger heaven! And cocktails? Well.. I fondly remember the Bloody Mary sorting me right out just before the Langkawi ferry last year, but tonight I started with a classic Moscow Mule and then superstar bar guru, Prakash suggested I go off piste with his own creation - the Ginger Mojito. And proper lush it was too! To be clear, it's not on the menu, but I'm sure if you ask him nicely, and say hi from me, he'll do you one!Can't rate Junk highly enough!

Author: Grace Lam
Review: Utterly forgettable meal. The restaurant aspires to “fine dining” but falls short in taste and service. The courses incorporated good ingredients, poorly used (think mayo on scallops, crab meat so indiscriminately mashed into risotto that …MoreUtterly forgettable meal. The restaurant aspires to “fine dining” but falls short in taste and service. The courses incorporated good ingredients, poorly used (think mayo on scallops, crab meat so indiscriminately mashed into risotto that its presence was obliterated by the taste of Parmesan). The food by itself is passable enough to deserve 2.5 stars but the high price of the set menu relative to the quality drags it down to one. Went on New Year’s Eve, which was probably why there was a live band playing Vegas tunes, which might have been forgivable if 1) we were in a bar, and 2) we hadn’t been seated within arm’s length of the band. When we asked to be moved, the waiter looked puzzled and obstinately refused, saying the seating arrangements were already fixed. Georgetown has enough cheap and mid-priced good restaurants and food stalls that you don’t need to go here. For a sit-down dining experience that beats it in price, service, and taste, I’d suggest going to Malaya Dining Room instead.
Location: Cheong Fatt Tze Mansion, 14, Lebuh Leith, Georgetown, George Town, Penang

Author: Adrian Cheah
Review: Traditional Malay cooking at Lagenda Café in the heart of George TownTrue to its name, Lagenda Café offers a host of  legendary Malay cuisines as …MoreTraditional Malay cooking at Lagenda Café in the heart of George TownTrue to its name, Lagenda Café offers a host of  legendary Malay cuisines as well as some Oriental and Western-fusion dishes. I usually go straight for the main course and skip the appetisers as the main dishes are hearty and I like to keep some room for the yummy desserts. The local favourites are surely top on my recommended list. Here are three fulfilling chicken dishes I would relish –  ayam percik madu tiga, belalang chicken rendang and ayam penyet Nusantara. Three brilliant ways of cooking chicken, each with its own distinct flavours. Ayam percik madu tiga is my daughter's favourite dish at this café. The smoky flavour of the aromatic grilled chicken marinated with savoury  peanut sauce has won her heart over. This dish is served with turmeric rice, jelatah (pickled vegetables), kerabu tauge (bean sprouts salad) and crackers. The belalangs chicken rendang is also very good. The thick fragrant curry owing to the generous use of coconut milk hugely complements the tender chicken and ulam (fresh greens such as winged beans) that accompanied this dish. On the congkak board of goodies you have something green, something spicy, something sour and something crispy – all enjoyed with a serving of warm blue rice. If you enjoy crispy fried chicken, go for the ayam penyet Nusantara. Chicken marinated with herbs and spices is deep-fried and served with blue-coloured rice, clear soup spiced with jintan (anise) and fried shallots, crackers and a lovely congkak board of ulam.The prawn lemak with pineapple is a rice set complete with a congkak-board of condiments (such as winged beans, pickled cucumber, kerabu omelette and sambal). Rice dyed blue with butterfly-pea flowers is wrapped in banana leaf to keep it moist and warm. Beautifully presented, the star of this dish, prawns are cooked in a typical Malay masak lemak fashion of coconut milk and turmeric. The creamy curry is sweetened with ripened pineapples, adding more depth to the flavours.As for desserts, panna cotta seri muka is a must-try item. The pandan-flavored custard is served with a drizzle of strawberry sauce. Please remind the waiter to serve the sauce on the side or to drizzle less if you prefer the level of sweetness to be reduced. Meanwhile on the side of this dessert are two scoops of blood-red glutinous rice. The sago do re mi (named after P. Ramlee's popular classic, Laksamana Do Re Mi) – three scoops of coloured sago pearls smothered with rich coconut cream and topped with fragrant palm sugar syrup – is a delicious treat. The banana bakar – grilled bananas topped with freshly grated coconut, brown sugar and a scoop of vanilla ice cream – is my favourite dessert. The combination of flavours and texture are so simple yet brilliant. Relish this to complete a satisfying meal here.Lagenda Café pays homage to Malaysia’s iconic musician P. Ramlee. You would notice some of the menu items are named after his famous works. The warm, cosy interior with an eclectic mix of furniture and paintings makes this a simply affordable café and a wonderful place to enjoy a meal or even drinks. The friendly staff have always made my visit pleasant and memorable. If you are touring George Town and would like to take a break and escape the tropical heat, Lagenda Café is an ideal choice. The café offers an extensive beverage list complete with fresh juices to mocktails and refreshing local delights. As you sip your drinks, take joy in P. Ramlee's melodious tunes that would effortlessly soothe your mind and soul.

The pre-war building in which Jawi House located is beautifully decorated with pictures of family and Jawi Peranakan ladies who were the frontier of their unique heritage. Review: Taj Wellington, opens its doors for Non Residents with its all new cafe , Hello Mews Cafe! …MoreTaj Wellington, opens its doors for Non Residents with its all new cafe , Hello Mews Cafe!As I step into this place, I am welcomed the Taj way with the Arti and Garland. It would be perfect in winters.Now I move onto my table and they have set a beautiful bouquet of pink roses on the table.Then I head onto read the menu. It is a pretty comprehensive one. From all day breakfast to Continental to Indian, there was something for all.For breakfast they had  the Taj bakery , Fresh cut fruit, paratha, idli and more.We started with  Hummus ₹385. The hummus was delicious absolutely.They have Salads small and large ₹350/₹550 .They did have Sandwiches too which we gave a miss.We moved onto have the pizza and loved it. It is for ₹750. What we liked that the onions were charred and not put raw. The tomato sauce was super fresh.Next up we tried Pesto linguine for ₹600, which was so delicious. It was a very good pesto I had in a long time. Also it was very filling.They did have Continental grills too. We tried one of their wellness dishes :Super food salad : quinoa , sweet potato , veere root , orange and citrus dressing . I loved it. The citrus dressing went so well with the whole salad.They did have Comfort Indian food too like Biryani , baingan bharta, Paneer Kathi rollNext up we tried Desserts for ₹385We had the Chocolate brownie . It was Uber delicious.They also have Thali and kiddies menu.For drinks we tried from the Jiva spa menuWe called for a Fruit juiceIron man (apples, guava, pear)Powered with antioxidant , rich in diner , iron , vitamin A , vitamin C. Absolutely refreshing.We called for Vegetable juice too.Celery , carrot , apple juiceNatural healing drink with low saturated fat .I really like juices so I loved it.Also what I liked was that it was so fresh with zero sugar or anything. Just made and given to us.They had a wide range of teas ₹300 like Kahwa, taj house blend , jasmine tea .We went outside to seat by the open area. We called for cappuccino and Americano, loved both.To mention the sweetest part, they got me a bouquet of red roses just to make it special. It is all about these little things they say.Kudos to the staff for hosting us!Tejendra, Shubham , Shruti , Shabbar , Sagar, Chinmayee !If you are looking for a gorgeous laid back night or a chilled out brunch amidst a decor which makes you feel at a luxury home, say hello to Muse Cafe!

Author: Iise Chew
Review: This is a place that epitomizes authenticity - be it the food with its palatable home-made fusion recipes, or the live music at its finest, or simply the amazing company and homely vibes exuding from the people here, it makes for an amazing …MoreThis is a place that epitomizes authenticity - be it the food with its palatable home-made fusion recipes, or the live music at its finest, or simply the amazing company and homely vibes exuding from the people here, it makes for an amazing experience.To me, what makes this place stand out is the close-knit community that has been formed here. While I was taking photographs of D'Loovi's, a young gentleman walked in, and multiple times was he greeted cheerfully with the same question - 'How was Langkawi?!'. Everyone in D'Loovi's knew him; everyone pretty much knew each other. They laughed like old buddies, shared their stories; it was a very pleasant vibe. In time, others coming in D'Loovi's joined the throng. Musicians, office workers, and people of various occupations made this a welcoming community. The owner of this place, by the name of Kelvin D'Loovi, makes for a most friendly and genuine person.I enjoy music thoroughly, and I love how the violin is prominently displayed here (I am a violinist myself). The music sensation is strong, where musicians often gather here for live performances. Reading the reviews online, live music is often mentioned to be amazing here. I sadly have yet to experience the music scene here, as the Movement Control Order due to COVID-19 has had the wings of fellow musicians clipped. That will have to be an experience for another time.For dinner, I was recommended the home-cooked mutton rendang - and boy, it was impeccably prepared. Simply superb. Kelvin himself ensures that the dishes served are up to standard. When I requested for no Cole-slaw, he whipped up stir-fried vegetables with bitter gourd, and that, surprisingly, perfectly complemented the mutton rendang. As I previously mentioned, this place serves home-made fusion recipes at its finest.I don't at all drink alcohol, but the non-alcoholic beverages were splendid. Fresh juices and mocktails are readily available. They're constantly coming with new ideas for their menu, and I was recommended the vanilla milkshake. A little bit on the sweet side, but still, kudos to the innovation the team here has.D'Loovi's is beautifully designed. It boasts a majestic exterior of what looks to be grand pillars, with an entrance seemingly hidden to the eye. Enter the door and you behold an epiphany of colours, music instruments, and trinkets placed in an orderliness that complements the vibes of this place.I have a strong aversion towards cigarette smoke (being a doctor, oh well), and I love how the interior of D'Loovi's is a non-smoking area. Should one wish to smoke (which of course, I would discourage), there is an allocated balcony outside which comprises of an artfully designed garden.If you are into great live music, or into finding communities as such, this is the place to be at. Authentic music, authentic food, authentic people - that's D'Loovi's.
Location: 24, Lebuh Melayu, Georgetown, George Town, Penang

Author: Edwin Ting
Review: Excellent dining experience with Baba Jerry and Nyonya Su Pei. They hosted our family (2 adults and 2 kids) in their private dining home / office. The dishes were all hand crafted and made by themselves using the freshest ingredients in a …MoreExcellent dining experience with Baba Jerry and Nyonya Su Pei. They hosted our family (2 adults and 2 kids) in their private dining home / office. The dishes were all hand crafted and made by themselves using the freshest ingredients in a homely Nyonya style.The dinner started with a Pandan and chlorophyll drink to cleanse the palette and whet the appetite. Followed by snacks of homemade fish cracker with special chilli sauce dip and pickled mango.Then we started the main dishes of Salted egg cereal chicken, crisp and fragrant and chicken that was tender yet meaty. The rempah pork with potato was absolutely delicious, tasted like an Indian spice curry, but made only with rempah. Stir fried choy sim was fresh and sweet with a hint of garlic and oyster sauce flavour. The fish, was the highlight, steamed in Cantonese style and garnished with carrot, chilli, cong and sesame seeds. The sauce was unami!! Made from a secret home recipe of home fermented soy sauce. Wrapping up the meal with a bonus dessert of pulut terigu, with fragrant coconut milk and barley.The best part of the meal was the casual sharing by Baba Jerry on cooking tips, health tips and even dining and shopping tips to find the best ingredients in Penang and Singapore.Baba Jerry and Nyonya Su Pei also teaches in Singapore at The Kitchen Society and host Private Dining Sessions in SG. If you are looking for an authentic Nyonya dining experience, be sure to follow them on FB / INS and at The Kitchen Society.
Restaurant: Nyonya Su Pei Private Dining / Heritage Artisans
Location: 53, Jalan Padang Victoria, George Town, Penang

Review: Fairly small, popular, booking should be considered, restaurant with basic but stylish layout & fittings with good background music setting an agreeable atmosphere. I love duck so I am in the right place. There are lunchtime set menus as …MoreFairly small, popular, booking should be considered, restaurant with basic but stylish layout & fittings with good background music setting an agreeable atmosphere. I love duck so I am in the right place. There are lunchtime set menus as well as ala carte with Asian & Western food styles. There are plenty of duck free options if desired. As well as food there is a fairly extensive array of soft beverages & a few beers as well. I had the Balinese Crispy Duck which was delicious. The skin was indeed very crisp & most of the fat had been cooked out of the meat although it was still moist. The hot sauce (not so hot by Malaysian standards) was served on the side so you could add to suit. There is quite an array of exotic desserts, I had special ice cream with caramel sauce which was quite good. The service was relaxed & friendly. I will return for more duck.

Author: Mark Doctoroff
Review: A wonderful, chef owned restaurant!We are "great friends of duck dishes" and this restaurant impressed us, and our 6 friends... The central location.. and "Nagor Street" with its many …MoreA wonderful, chef owned restaurant!We are "great friends of duck dishes" and this restaurant impressed us, and our 6 friends... The central location.. and "Nagor Street" with its many restaurants, bakeries, bars etc. creates a "wonderful vibe" as one approaches this "hidden gem". It is equally pleasant for lunch or supper.... The dishes include several very affordable set meals [which include appetizers, soup a main dish and drink]... as well as "a la carte" specialties. This chef owned restaurant puts wonderful food and the guest first... and this leads to great service with a most "memorable meal". The servers are also very helpful in explaining the various options. The ambience of the restaurant makes a long, leisurely meal very comfortable. TripAdvisor has awarded it the "Certificate of Excellence"... and it is highly rated by travellers and locals [it in the top 1% of restaurants in Georgetown]. Its definitely worthy of a visit!I hope that this Review has been helpful!

Review: Heaps of praises for the food - mushroom soup was tasty with chunky bits although hubby commented he would like it thicker, duck confit was melt in your mouth tender from skin to meat and the honey glazed duck was lovely. The duck pasta was …MoreHeaps of praises for the food - mushroom soup was tasty with chunky bits although hubby commented he would like it thicker, duck confit was melt in your mouth tender from skin to meat and the honey glazed duck was lovely. The duck pasta was amazing too - aromatic and full of flavours. Ambience was cozy and the heritage vibe in the area kept things interesting. Would have given a 5-star if the waiter who served us on 20th June evening could have been more patient and helpful with our orders. We asked what he would recommend as it was our first time visiting and he said recommendations are in the menu. When we further asked which was more popular - duck confit or honey glazed, he replied you can try both! We only wanted to order one main btw. We chose the honey glazed. But when our meals came, he served us both. Kind of a blessing really as we are returning for the duck confit. But, service could really be better at WTD in Jalan Nagore, Penang.

Review: Dindugal doesn't dissapoint!Despite having read several negative reviews of this place on Google Review, my …MoreDindugal doesn't dissapoint!Despite having read several negative reviews of this place on Google Review, my husband decided to go with his gut-feel and we stepped into the restaurant for our breakfast of Dindigul Biryani ~ the first time we were ever having biryani in the morning. Portions were moderate and more than enough for each person. The chicken dish initially looked like it wouldn't be sufficient but surprisingly it was!Our total brunch came up to about RM80 but I would say it was value for money. The waiters were also friendly & helpful with suggestions.Point here is, while reviews are helpful, don't always let it be the deciding factor when trying out a new restaurant. Sometimes, you just might be pleasantly surprised with what you get!Thank you Dindigul Restaurant for the lovely brunch before we started our sight-seeing of beautiful Penang! 🙂

The masala tea was good and the parotta was buttery and good as well, but I didn’t come here for parotta and tea, I came for the biriyani and the other main dishes.

Review: I rarely leave reviews but felt that I had to this time because I am very disappointed with my experience at Il Bacaro. …MoreI rarely leave reviews but felt that I had to this time because I am very disappointed with my experience at Il Bacaro.To start, the food was okay (not the best Italian that I've had but acceptable and decently enjoyable). Towards the end of my meal however, I found a dead insect (I believe a fly) in one of the clams served in my pasta (vongole). You may see the image attached. Seeing it really ruined my appetite and made the meal less appetising immediately.Having said that though, I understand that mistakes/accidents happen, and I wanted to inform someone immediately so they could be more attentive next time. I imagined that anyone running a respectable restaurant would have wanted to be informed, and be apologetic about the incident. Instead, the owner's response was shocking to me. She just looked at it, mumbled something along the lines of, "I suppose that happened sometime during the cooking..Sorry!" nonchalantly and just walked away! Her entire response was less than 3 seconds; she was completely unbothered by it.She did not take my plate or the fly away, or sound in the least bit sorry. In fact, her response was borderline rude. For a restaurant of this supposed caliber, I thought that she would perhaps offer a complimentary dessert, or at the very very least, be sincerely concerned and apologetic about an incident like this.The only saving grace was that (entirely dissatisfied with her response), when we later informed one of the male waiters, he was much more apologetic and immediately assured us that he would inform the chef of this occurrence.The owner's behaviour was sincerely distasteful and in my opinion, unacceptable. Mistakes happen and that's understandable, but the way one responses is crucial, and her response ruined our evening.Overall, I'd recommend that you spend your money elsewhere. There are plenty of other great eateries in Penang.  Il Bacaro's food is average and service leaves much to be desired.
Location: Campbell House, 106, Lebuh Campbell, Georgetown, George Town, Penang

I specifically told the waiter to decan the red as it would appreciate allowable time to breathe.Our food came, the antipasto....we dug in and feast. One of the cheese were dry and every bite leave a flak mark, this is not quite palatable mate! Well, we raised this up and an exchange of blue cheese was given to us. Cool...we love it.Then came our hot food...the gnocchi zafferano. Ohh....it's one of the least acceptable to an average quality. It's soft, somewhat soggy..... probably over boiled/cooked. Nothing like the gnocchi from Sassorosso and Osteria Italian restaurante in Kuala Lumpur. These 2 restaurants gave good Aldante pasta (cook just right) and a good munch.Lastly, came our redwine which we ordered. As requested, the redwine supposed to be decan! But it wasn't done. The restaurant closes at 11pm but they allow us to sit until we exhaust the wine which it's kind of them.Alright, hopefully to see improvement or was I just unlucky.

However it is always a shame when a restraunt cannot receive the review it deserves due to it's service.We were told we could sit inside when there was a table available. Even after two tables were free, my girlfriend and I realised that the lady at the front had completely forgotten us. After waiting another twenty minutes I asked the waiter if we could sit inside and he promptly made the table and apologised for his colleagues oversight.The only problem is the excuse he gave me. "Sorry sir we were busy today". I'm sorry, but for such a really small restaurant, this cannot be an excuse. If anything, due to the size of your establishment, you should be twice as attentive.Anyways, all in all the food was good, and I have tried to be as constructive as I can. The chefs deserve at least a 4 or. 4.5 out of 5 but leaving us outside for almost an hour is inexcusable. Based on your food I'll recommend you to others but I advise you tell your staff to get their act together.

Author: David Chew
Review: Nonya restaurants serve a romantic nostalgia of the times when meals were always cooked at home, where mothers slaved in the kitchen, preparing the ingredients, cooking them meticulously to produce a taste that's unmistakably home. …MoreNonya restaurants serve a romantic nostalgia of the times when meals were always cooked at home, where mothers slaved in the kitchen, preparing the ingredients, cooking them meticulously to produce a taste that's unmistakably home.However, not all nonya restaurants are equal, just as each home had its own tweak on the basic recipes. Auntie Gaik Lean's endeavours to bring the best of these home flavours to their dishes, and it works, as can be seen by the glowing reviews here.I have known Auntie Gaik Lean for many years now, even when she was a proprietor of her previous shop in Petaling Jaya - The Long Table. Since then, I was already a fan of her cooking and was disappointed when The Long Table closed its doors for good.Nestled at the junction of Bishop Street and Beach Street, it's housed in what used to be BP DeSilva, a jewellery shop. The shop has taken great pains not to remove the glory of the previous tenants and hints can be seen everywhere.The dining area is a comfortably sized room, and large tables with lazy Susans on top of them. An immediate sense of nostalgia hits you as you enter this room, with the window displays of nostalgic everyday items, including a Honda C50.Parking here can be a bit of a problem during weekdays due to its location in the business district of Penang. Weekends offer a respite to this as parking spaces are aplenty along Bishop Street.The extensive menu offers the typical nonya fare, and then some. Do ask if there are any specials that may be on offer, as these items are not on the menu and are truly special one off dishes that are rarely found anywhere else.From the constant flow of guests in and out, a sense of confidence will pervade that you have made the right choice for sampling their nonya dishes.While some complain about the prices, I have found it to be very reasonable - after all, one can't place a price on going back in time and enjoying the fond memories of savouring the home-cooked goodness from the kitchens in our homes.Definitely a winner - and you won't go wrong picking this place as your go to for really authentic nonya dishes. Bar none.
Restaurant: Auntie Gaik Lean's Old School Eatery
Location: 1, Bishop St, George Town, Pulau Pinang

We ordered a menu of inche kabin, fish curry, ju hu char, sweet sambal brinjals, egg belanda and assam prawns.We ordered at about 8.05pm and the first dish arrived way past 8.30pm although there were only five occupied tables. The dishes that arrived were ju hu char,  inche kabin, sambal brinjal and egg belanda. The fish curry and assam prawns came later after a reminder. We were shocked at the portion of fish served such that the dish was full with fish fillet and lacking in curry sauce. The photo showed how much of the fish that had to be bagged home. We were so famished by then, we dug into the food immediately without snapping any photos. 😅Upon payment at the counter, in response to our feedback, the curt response was how many people were in your party, we can add more curry sauce for you and the turn-off bit - 'never mind, its the new year'. As someone with experience in the food/service industry, I'd had expected a simple apology:  'sorry for the unpleasant experience, your feedback is appreciated, we will remind our order staff to be more attentive in future and confirm the portion desired by customers.'As a Penang-born and someone with Peranakan family members who are cooks, the only dishI  found worthy of the standard of an established nonya eatery was the egg belanda.In the hospitality industry, we believe in continuous service improvement and I hope the management  receive this feedback in the same spirit to preserve their service in this competitive industry.

Author: Adrian Cheah
Review: The Ferringhi Garden Restaurant: great dining within an oasisThe Ferringhi Garden Restaurant has an amazing lush garden filled with flowers …MoreThe Ferringhi Garden Restaurant: great dining within an oasisThe Ferringhi Garden Restaurant has an amazing lush garden filled with flowers in full bloom. Even before looking through the menu, we could not resist taking a few photographs of its tranquil and beautiful dining ambience. My family and I were having dinner with our hosts, Dato' Welf and Datin Susan. After a few snaps, we returned to our table and were ready for a delectable feast.For starters, we had a charcoal-toasted sourdough loaf served with garlic aioli and tomato salsa, smoked salmon with pink potato cubes and tomato salad as well as mushroom soup. All were so delicious and we waited in anticipation for our main courses.Susan and my wife decided to go for the Australian sirloin. The generous cuts were premium grade strip steaks cooked to perfection over a flaming charcoal fire. The intense, smoky, fire-seared flavours infused in the steaks added character and depth to the dish. Both were very pleased with their scrumptious meals. Welf selected the Australian beef tenderloin, a tender cut of fillet mignon served with roasted vegetables and mashed potatoes. His steak had a salty, crispy exterior and a tender, juicy, medium-rare centre. The chef served the accompanying sauce in a mini pan, taking great care not to smother the steak. I had the passion fruit snapper – a sous vide red snapper fillet with passion fruit sabayon and bell pepper ratatouille. The combination of flavours was refreshing and this was the first time I had the passion fruit sabayon with fish! Kudos to the chef for this creative dish.For dessert, Welf and my wife had the decadent double chocolate tart made of 70 per cent Belgian dark chocolate. It was served with a scoop of raspberry and mint sorbet. This dessert was rich yet refreshing, tangy yet sweet, creamy yet crunchy; all so very exciting in the same mouthful. My daughter happily indulged in a serving of dark chocolate brownie – a 70 per cent dark Belgian chocolate cake topped with a sinfully-delicious salted caramel macadamia gelato. It was indeed a brilliant choice to conclude a wonderful dinner.The service at Ferringhi Garden Restaurant was excellent and the time flew by very quickly especially when we were having such an enjoyable dinner. I was very glad we were able to indulge in such a simple pleasures of life – good food and great company. Thanks you, Welf and Susan, for a memorable evening.P.S. Be selective so that you savour the best choices on offer!
Location: 34, Jalan Batu Ferringhi, Kampung Batu Feringgi, Batu Ferringhi, Pulau Pinang

Review: This is essentially THE ONLY Batu Ferringhi restaurant worth going to,  if you care about & appreciate good food. The thing about Batu Ferringhi is that there is definitely no shortage of places to eat at,  and a typical restaurant/cafe …MoreThis is essentially THE ONLY Batu Ferringhi restaurant worth going to,  if you care about & appreciate good food. The thing about Batu Ferringhi is that there is definitely no shortage of places to eat at,  and a typical restaurant/cafe will have 70-100 items on their menu to choose from, but the quality is mediocre at best in most cases. Sure,  you will pay next to nothing but you will also get nothing of value,  regardless of the restaurant's decor, neon signs,  and marketing hype online. The Ferringhi Garden & Coffee is minimalist in its menu,  but truly delivers quality F&B items,  backed by very friendly service staff, and really fast service! The place feels like the Garden of Eden with countless plants and flowers, and a few waterfalls scattered around for a relaxing dining atmosohere. Prices here are above the typical Batu Ferringhi outlet,  but you will receive unequalled food,  beverage,  and service. Don't waste your money and precious vacation time with other food courts & cafes, just come here and enjoy great food in an unmatched ambiance.

The candle on my table wasn't even lit until I told the other waiter to do it...Don't get me wrong, the environment and food are top notch and worth the price. Author: Khooala Lumpur
Review: Authentic assam laksa, one of the better ones in Penang. Pair it with some lobak, and quench your thirst with some iced cold sugar cane juice from the stalls nearby. So refreshing.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: J C
Review: There is a push cart store here that sells cheap and delicious and juicy durian. Be sure to drop by if you want to taste different kind of durian in Penang. We were charged 15RM per kg for the durian. But just be aware that u might not have the most clean place to eat or wash up after eating.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: rindhi widyastuti
Review: Some said the laksa sauce/soup was too fishy, but i still can manage it in my tongue 😄 and the laksa mie was so good and chewy 💖 the place is in the side road, in the side of air itam market.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Razelyn
Review: Best laksa i had in penang. Thick and savoury fish broth with the herbs makes this a perfect bowl of assam laksa. A must try eatery when in penang.The owner is so passionate in what he is doing and think this is the secret recipe of this flavourful noodles.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: bay hanlin (zacbhl)
Review: Ordered the small bowl for RM4.50. The stall front had some article about the stall, and you can see most tables ordering this dish. We tried it ourselves and found the broth to be quite subtle and enjoyable. The noodles were soft and chewy that went well with the sardines and onions.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Luke Phang
Review: THE assam laksa that made Penang famous all around the world, though the queue can get quite long and the seating is far from comfortable. Protip: There are seats opposite the stall in the market. …MoreTHE assam laksa that made Penang famous all around the world, though the queue can get quite long and the seating is far from comfortable. Protip: There are seats opposite the stall in the market.Cheap and superb tasting. Just be sure to allocate wait time up to 30 minutes during peak periods. Only open in the day time, closed in the evening and night.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Steven
Review: One of the best Laksa in Penang. Very popular among the locals and tourists. Do expect a long queue.The laksa broth is very thick and tasty, with a lot of fish meat in it.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Joshua Ratcliff
Review: Love these one dish establishments. No hassle, just turn up and eat a delicious, cheap meal. This was the best Assam Laksa I tried in Penang.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Yihui Low
Review: Definitely worth a visit. Penang laksa gives you a wide range of flavours all in our mouthful. And they have it all right. Giving it a 4 starts because there were housefly all over the place while we we there. There is a drain right by the stall as well. Not for the weak tummies.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Said Azlan
Review: BEST LAKSA I'VE EVER HAD.. the broth is nice and thick but not too heavy due to the mints that they add on to the dish. really worth your time and appetite to experience this dish.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Rachel Yeoh
Review: The laksa and the sugar cane juice are perfect match. Not easy to find another stall who can beat this asam laksa, it is so good.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Nicholas Kang
Review: Not really my kind of dish because I'm not the biggest fan of Assam laksa, but it's still worth trying as one of the many stops to try long Air Itam. The texture of the noodles were amazing!
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Wailim Ho
Review: Excellent Assam Laksa that kept original evergreen taste for all these years.  Smooth rice vermicelli, thick laksa broth served with generous portion of shredded fish meat, shrimp paste, sliced onion and ginger flower bud. Expect lots of …MoreExcellent Assam Laksa that kept original evergreen taste for all these years.  Smooth rice vermicelli, thick laksa broth served with generous portion of shredded fish meat, shrimp paste, sliced onion and ginger flower bud. Expect lots of crowd, as the stall is basically a hole-in-wall stall beside a market place  environment comfort and hygiene needs getting used to.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Ed Thayer
Review: This was a site I visited during one of many visits to Penang. I discovered the eatery on an episode of Anthony Bourdain. I traveled to nearly every restaurants Tony visited and this place did not let me down. I even have a photo of myself sitting at Tony's table.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Cynthia Wan
Review: It’s a small bowl, but satisfying, and some may want seconds.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Victor Khor
Review: Update: 5 Feb 2022:-During MCO, it announced stall will be closed for good. After MCO, it only open on weekend and closed during weekday. God knows why. …MoreUpdate: 5 Feb 2022:-During MCO, it announced stall will be closed for good. After MCO, it only open on weekend and closed during weekday. God knows why.Now, during CNY, price has increased to RM5.50 per bowl.Profitability from the people should not be a priority at this point despite not operate for months during MCO. You must have gained alot already over the last 20-30years. Consistency and food quality should be the priority so people will not continue to criticise your food and price.Food: Only Assam LaksaAmbiance: stall at the roadside, hot and humid. Be prepare to sweat. Open from 10am to 7pmPrice: Steadily increased over the years. From RM2 to now RM5 per bowl.Service: Will be served at the table. Pay when served. Takeaway is availableOverall: Could be the 3rd generation running this business. Su Koay Th'ng sweet dessert (see pic) stall located next to Assam Laksa stall is a steal.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Alderina Gracia
Review: This place is busy but the whole family is ready for work! My chopstick was falling and 2 servers were promptly giving me replacement. Defintely very nice Assam Laksa: fish shredded broth and shrimp paste, amazing combination! And a bit tangi from lemon?
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Munraj Gill
Review: the best laksa in penang, it tastes so fresh and tasty. can be hard to get a seat, but totally worth it.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: JJ Z
Review: The best Assam Laksa in town, place has limited tables and chairs so depend on timing, u might need wait for a while, serving is good for one, just nice.  A must try if you in town!
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: peter liew
Review: I've never liked and eaten it because of the heavy fishy that associate with it. But this is first time I have it and is very delicious. …MoreI've never liked and eaten it because of the heavy fishy that associate with it. But this is first time I have it and is very delicious.It not fishy at all. The soup is tangy, sweet and fragrant with ginger flower and it loaded with mint. Noodle is soft. Highly recommended. Cost RM5 per bowl. Business hour 10.30am till 7pm.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Goh Wah
Review: Taste OK, there are stalls with better taste, lesser crowd and better service elsewhere in Penang (e.g. Penang Road, BB Cafe in Bayan Baru, the Laksa stall in the food court opposite, Laksa stall in Balik Pulau, Kampung Pisang). The taste …MoreTaste OK, there are stalls with better taste, lesser crowd and better service elsewhere in Penang (e.g. Penang Road, BB Cafe in Bayan Baru, the Laksa stall in the food court opposite, Laksa stall in Balik Pulau, Kampung Pisang). The taste is a little on the sweet side. They could have put up signs on the ordering system (takeaway and eat in) to help the crowd, mostly tourist.  Price is reasonable for its portion and popularity.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: A
Review: I’m not really used to Assam Laksa, don’t expect it to be similar to regular laksa!! Unique taste :)
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Elaine
Review: The most visited Laksa food stall at Penang! Although this place is always crowded but I confirm is worth the waitsss. Plus, there's a uncle selling peanut-mochi, sweet and soft mochi, you must give it a try too!
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Melissa M
Review: Talk about flavor!! There is so much happening in this bowl but you can still taste the individual flavors of the vegetables. …MoreTalk about flavor!! There is so much happening in this bowl but you can still taste the individual flavors of the vegetables.Given the amount of ingredients and different pastes and sauces in it, it is not for the weak of heart. Come hungry and ready for the heat to build (if your a westerner).The sugar cane juice stall cools it down nicely.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Alex Chiang
Review: Tried the Penang Famous Pasar Air Iran Laksa. Taste is balance! Overall is not too bad. Can improve on the overall environment! If you don’t mind the street feel, food is recommended. It’s usually packed and have to wait for seats. Worth a try but can do without!
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Alicia Lum
Review: Not a fan of assam laksa. It cost RM4.80 for a bowl. Service is quick and fuss free. I find it too spicy and sour for my liking. The noodle portion was also quite little. Maybe the flavours just isn't for me. It is quite to find, less than 10 minutes walk from Kek Lok Si Temple.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Andrew Chan (www.roadtrippers.asia)
Review: Iconic Penang Assam Laksa stall - great tasting food - nice balance of taste.Price wise is OK .. quite a value for money bowl of noodles. …MoreIconic Penang Assam Laksa stall - great tasting food - nice balance of taste.Price wise is OK .. quite a value for money bowl of noodles.Only draw back for this stall is parking - pretty difficult to get a parking even on a normal day.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: earlyreflections3
Review: Ahhh yes the classic. Anthony Bourdains favourite Asam Laksa and for good reason. Super savoury, salty and fragrant this is a must! Not the usual sweet version but if you're more into savoury flavours this laksa won't be beat!
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Jeff See
Review: Very unique local street food. This is the creme la creme of laksa caterer. It has changed its business hours due to covid 19 pandemic. Life has not been the same since. One can taste the best during weekend only for the time being. Let's pray we get to go back to the same old days soon.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Wira dharmawan
Review: Authentic laksa,a bit far to reach from city but it pays off.If you are single individual dont mind shared a table with another individual coz they are coming with the same purposed laksa.😂
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Jeen Lin Ng
Review: This was supposedly the BEST assam laksa in Penang, the most famous one. It was meant to be the highlight meal for our Penang trip. Disappointingly their standard has apparently dropped recently: the soup was watery with disintegrated fish, …MoreThis was supposedly the BEST assam laksa in Penang, the most famous one. It was meant to be the highlight meal for our Penang trip. Disappointingly their standard has apparently dropped recently: the soup was watery with disintegrated fish, flavour not very prominent, noodles didn't have a slight bite to it. On the upside there was a good balance of cucumber and mint in the bowl but that was really it. Give it 6/10 just for the food, but definitely not good enough to return once you factor in the longish drive (40 mins from George Town), long wait for food and wrestle for tables.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Kh Wan
Review: Tried many Penang laksas but this still tops my list. Texture of the soup is thicker and more flavourful. Definately worth the GRAB here.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Preston Ng
Review: portion very small so one bowl sure not enough. Old man (chef) will happily take picture with you. excellent to eat asam laksa during hot sunny climate. Asam laksa is sour and spicy. May be too exotic for westerners' taste buds.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: roden zheng
Review: Most of local people's said that the laksa its very nice, but we have 6 persons and can't finished 3 bowls of laksa. Location very near kek lok shi temple
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Tony Ng
Review: tasted not as good as before and bit expensive for a bowl of LAKSA but for those have not tried Penang Assam Laksa worth trying
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: wong engwah
Review: I must say it's not everyone cuppa tea. Some may really like it's authentic flavour and rural ambience, others may not feel affinity with meal or place. It's very crowded, parking is notoriously difficult and getting there is a challenge.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Francis PHX
Review: Love the Assam Laksa and other food here 😍
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Nurul Winanda
Review: Sedapnya. Laksa air itam yang iconic. We had to wait for a while to be served. Worth the wait. The soup is umami. A must go if you're in Penang.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Joel
Review: The only original store. The broth is really unique and hearsay has been the same for a really long time. I have asked the owner about the broth and it is based on sardine. Not spicy at all, with lots of mint leaves on top. At the end i …MoreThe only original store. The broth is really unique and hearsay has been the same for a really long time. I have asked the owner about the broth and it is based on sardine. Not spicy at all, with lots of mint leaves on top. At the end i don't really know if i like it or not but it is unique. Will come back again for another try to decide if i do like it. By the road side at the three way junction, opposite the food court. Five ringgit per bowl.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Gary Lee
Review: For sure the best laksa in Penang ! Cheap price, fishy flavour, a must try if ur in Penang !
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Tina Liow
Review: One of the "must" go to street food laksa in Penang. The soup is thick with a balanced taste of sweet, sour and spicy, added with lingering touch of the prawn paste. It’s a small bowl, but satisfying.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Swan Yia Choy
Review: Pretty good. Decent mix of flavours and quite fragrant, but I feel like there's something missing from the broth. Almost perfect but not quite there
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Boey
Review: It has a favourable taste. With a bunch of mint leaf and chilli. Then, a little bit of spicy and the noodles bring a sweet sour taste. Nice. The price a bit high which is rm5. Normally the price is rm4 in other place
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Ray Cez
Review: Parking is really hard to find around this area.The laksa here is up to general standard, mixed feedback from what I have heard but I think they are very generous with the portion and it is tasty.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Quak Yong Sheng
Review: Tasty Assam laksa, the character of this bowl of laksa is it’s strong and pungent taste, if you like strong flavours its is a must try! Penang laksa should be like this in my opinion! :) tasty!
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Elsa Chung
Review: The one and only apparently. There are 2 stalls directly across from each other. If you are looking for the one that the late Anthony Bourdain visited, then make sure you are not on the market side. Look for a picture of Mr. Bourdain behind …MoreThe one and only apparently. There are 2 stalls directly across from each other. If you are looking for the one that the late Anthony Bourdain visited, then make sure you are not on the market side. Look for a picture of Mr. Bourdain behind the boiling laksa and you are in the correct stall.The asam broth is not the most flavourful, but one of the better ones we have had. The noodles were not overcooked, pieces of fish are swimming in a sea of red. RM4.80 a bowl.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Sam Fy
Review: I only think of this place if is come to asam laksa in Penang.Taste is still same. Price is cheap. Abit difficult to get a parking as is a tourist place and pasar located here. …MoreI only think of this place if is come to asam laksa in Penang.Taste is still same. Price is cheap. Abit difficult to get a parking as is a tourist place and pasar located here.But the environment is really dirty. Make sure you can handle it before you taste the food 😁
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: trin 17
Review: Forget ambience as it is at a wet market and hot as heck. To get a place to sit, i would say go after 3pm. Flavorful sour and spicy fish broth with noodles. Easily best assam laksa in this part of the world. Sugar cane drink was freshly juiced.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: adi antoro
Review: Love the crowd, food, and traditional market. Need a lil bit cleaning up. Laksa is quite unique
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Vikram Venu
Review: I have never had anything like this before, and I am now truly, deeply, in love.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Amel Desain
Review: Not my type, the mie is little sour and squid taste... no egg in bowl, if you want try asam laksa, just buy one and share with your friend here... i buy 4 (4people) and we cant eat this laksa.. very different with katong laksa in singapore..
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Shirley Sy
Review: Decent bowl of noodles and service was super fast. Got here at 11.30am, no queue and got served immediately. Soup is on the thin side, bit salty and very fishy so may not be for everyone but I enjoyed it. Not life changing but a good pit stop before heading up to the temple.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Hashwin Singh
Review: Tangy, slightly sweet and not as spicy as I expected but nevertheless enjoyed the dish very much. Goes well with a glass of sugar cane juice on a hot day. The staff were friendly and attentive as I merely had to signal for a bowl after …MoreTangy, slightly sweet and not as spicy as I expected but nevertheless enjoyed the dish very much. Goes well with a glass of sugar cane juice on a hot day. The staff were friendly and attentive as I merely had to signal for a bowl after seating myself and they served it in a jiffy. Worth a try if you're visiting the Kek Lok Si temple nearby.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: He Xiang
Review: Very strong tasting assam laksa. Not for everyone.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Kevern Yong
Review: assam laksa Tastes ok,this is the most popular laksa in Penang, Very close to the kek lok si temple
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Guan Meng Fong
Review: Been here twice this yesr. Asam Laksa was quite good, but standards seem to vary between the two visit. Once was excellent and the other was only above average. I would say worth a try if you are in this area. Parking and seating places can be difficult during peak hour.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: sze yah chng
Review: The fish smell very strong when u get closer, but interestingly u won’t feel the fish is not fresh when u eat. It is somehow very nice to eat. One bowl rm5 consider good in tourist attraction place . Worth trying
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: 张嘉妮
Review: I am very sad that every year I come the taste become lesser and lesser, I hope they can maintain the standard and make the taste thicker again. …MoreI am very sad that every year I come the taste become lesser and lesser, I hope they can maintain the standard and make the taste thicker again.Who know I feel fried lobak, dumpling and poh pia is nicer than asam laksa ...
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: K River
Review: Famous Penang laksa store by the side of the wet market. The laksa is a bit weak and watery. It is very reasonably priced at RM4.80 for a small bowl. This is not my favourite laksa store as there are better ones around.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Kong Ho (LaksaPaint)
Review: How a good asam laksa should be.   Refreshing and pack a punch of flavour.  Superfast service
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Jenny Tan
Review: Not as nice as it used to be but overall still okay. Most tourists will try out the Penang Air Itam laksa because it is so popular.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Scott Milliquet
Review: Excellent food.   Local sitting next to us said it was the best laksa in Malaysia.   I didn’t have better in the two weeks in Malaysia.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Ravindran Renganathan
Review: The best Laksa in Penang Island. Situated near the market may turn off some people but those who love good food will enjoy it. Along the road leading to the place, I came across a replica of trucks with soldiers, a reminder of the Japanese …MoreThe best Laksa in Penang Island. Situated near the market may turn off some people but those who love good food will enjoy it. Along the road leading to the place, I came across a replica of trucks with soldiers, a reminder of the Japanese occupation in Penang Island. Managed to take a photo of it while driving out after having a wonderful and tasty bowl of Laksa. The broth is rich and the flavor superb. 👍
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Jason
Review: Hot and crowded place but worth the wait if you love assam laksa
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Bon Heur
Review: nice laksa & loh bak, but stress to eat cause a lot customer look at you waiting your seat
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: B Saputra
Review: One of must eat delicacies in penang. If you like sour type of laksa, it’s definitely must try this one.Very cheap and abundant ingredients
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Willy Lim
Review: Penang Assam Laksa is an acquired taste. The dish with its fragrant (or pungent) prawn paste, a dash of peppermint, coupled with the sourish assam soup base, is sworn by many a connoisseur as worthy of being the signature dish of Penang.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: toxicburn1
Review: I'll just say, "ugliest" damn tastiest bowls of laksa :)Older gentlemen washed noodles in the broth and whipped up 2 bowls of laksa in under a minute. Flavor explosion in every spoon!
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Shereen Leong
Review: The authentic asam laksa. After 20 years the laksa taste still the same. Asam laksa plus sugar cane drink is superb.. this area is crowded, need to park far..
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Bee Teng
Review: Nice laksa and got fried food beside can eat also. Drink with 甘蔗水。👍
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Bradly Malitam
Review: Great place to get famous Penang laksa
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: virginia loke
Review: The best laksa in Penang! They located right beside the road. They have a proper shop beside them so don't need to wait for table. If you like laksa you must visit here and order 2 bowl of it!
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: William Pratama
Review: Taste: 7,5Place: 6Price: 7,5 …MoreTaste: 7,5Place: 6Price: 7,5Service: 8Finally got the chance to scoop this legend! Very fragrant, if you close your eyes it might trick you into thinking about thai food. I used to believe that this laksa along with it reputation should be on 10 points easy for the taste, but my preference tells another. If you happen to be indonesian, you can try laksa duri TSS, jembatan lima (jakarta), they got almost similar flavour.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Alvin Choong
Review: It's delicous and affordable. Parking space is a problem around there, so best to park at the carpark of the temple infront. Sharing of table would be a better choice if you do not mind. Didn't quite expected how it would taste as it suppose to have assam in it. Ordering from the staff and service was quick, highly recommended.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Tarisha Chahal
Review: Honestly nothing great about it.. not much flavour to it..I would prefer Ah Cheng Laksa anytime!
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Joshua Foo
Review: Have I reviewed this place before? Wait, err, no. If it was 5 - 10 years ago, I'll give it 5 stars plus, now the darling of penang laksa has slowly losing its shine. …MoreHave I reviewed this place before? Wait, err, no. If it was 5 - 10 years ago, I'll give it 5 stars plus, now the darling of penang laksa has slowly losing its shine.I'd give it 4 stars if they didn't use Angcle Peoh's photo as their trademark, who has since moved to Klang. But this place still serves at RM5 per bowl, despite they cut down on the portion.What it lacks is the chilli, pineapple that we so remembered the best original taste. And also the instant kick when you first taste it, let alone smell it. The broth is not so red as before too.Well, perhaps its penangites time to visit Klang and Angcle Peoh to judge for yourself, even though the pricier side, but with better ambiance and aircon.Will I be back? Sure, if I'm around PG.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Albert Sutiono
Review: Nice laksa, a little bit limited space to sit, but people tend to eat and go.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: kimberly lawlaw
Review: I’m pretty disappointed. The soup isn’t as nice as before 3 years back. Sugar cane is nice. The popiah isn’t very nice.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Gold 131
Review: RM 5 for laksa, RM 2 for sugar cane juice. Today less tourists @ 4 pm.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: lmt6618 *
Review: Located outside air itam wet market. This stall has been here over 30 years. Laksa was served with a sweet overtone. Food was served between 5-10 minutes. 30 years ago laksa had ommph...thick, spicy and loads of fish in broth. Seating is …MoreLocated outside air itam wet market. This stall has been here over 30 years. Laksa was served with a sweet overtone. Food was served between 5-10 minutes. 30 years ago laksa had ommph...thick, spicy and loads of fish in broth. Author: ARacking Shelving Solutions
Review: The Penang Laksa is great! Love it. Best with Fresh coconut on a super sunny day!
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Lichan Cheah
Review: The uncle here has been making Assam laksa here for decades. The soup is deep with flavour and the noodles are tender and delicious. Get a sugarcane juice for the most Malaysian food order ever.
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: Julian Futanto
Review: A great stretch of eateries always bustling with people. Good food albeit a little unclean. Try the chendol!
Location: Jalan Pasar, Paya Terubong, George Town, Penang

Author: James Munday
Review: Overall: Great little cafe and one of my favorite places to have breakfast in Penang right now. Whilst I really like it, its let down by high prices and dark interior. …MoreOverall: Great little cafe and one of my favorite places to have breakfast in Penang right now. Whilst I really like it, its let down by high prices and dark interior.Food: A mash of millennial inspired breakfast options from a full-English, to smashed avocado on wholemeal toast.  They have a few things that are difficult to find elsewhere : half decent bacon and a pork sausage, bratwurst style.Veggie friendly: Yes, they have stand-alone veggie options as well as a 'build your own' menu.Price: A bit expensive. Breakfast for 2 with some coffee can cost 80-90RM. Price is usually pumped up by pork and avocado, so cheaper options can be had, but its still on the high end for breakfast.Service: Order at the counter, deliver to the table.Atmosphere: I find it a bit dark inside. Its all wooden chairs and concrete and some of the rooms lack a bit of natural light. Out front is lovely with its plants. The back is nice, indoors, light and plants but then you're next to the toilets... needs a rethink. Open up some windows and get some light into the place!Location: Near the Chinese temple on Penang road.Amenities: There are toilets at the back. They're clean. The plastic door/tin roof arrangement doesn't quite match the price you're paying.Must try: The missus loves the Chai Latte. Personally, after being in a Muslim country so long, I love the pork sausage - everywhere else is usually chicken.

Author: Richard Benjamin 'Tsard' Chua
Review: I was actually just walking along the street in my quest for a hearty brunch, with a craving for toasts and eggs, which I seem to not find in the Indian cafés in the area. Seeing the interior ambience from the street invited me to come in, …MoreI was actually just walking along the street in my quest for a hearty brunch, with a craving for toasts and eggs, which I seem to not find in the Indian cafés in the area. Seeing the interior ambience from the street invited me to come in, and I knew right away that this is the answer to my craving. The service crew immediately flashed their smiles as I came in, and from then I knew this will be a good brunch for me! The lady who took my order was radiating with warmth, I felt very welcome.I got an iced caramel latte (14MYR) and a full plate of toasts, eggs, sausages, plus coleslaw and baked beans (16.50MYR). I am indeed satisfied with my brunch! There's plenty of sumptuous items on the menu, but my stomach cannot afford more than what I got. I don't think there's room for a sweet dessert, until I, maybe, walked for a couple of kilometres.Ambience is very relaxing, taking it from it's old-world-ish charm of exposed brick walls, marble floors, high ceilings, natural light flowing in, cool air-conditioning (feels like ~35°C outside), wooden furniture, and the greens incorporated within. I must give commendation to the house music, as well—very fitting with everything around. All these, spells the word CHILLAX. Definitely a must-visit spot when in this area of Pinang.
Location: 35, Jalan Masjid Kapitan Keling, Georgetown, George Town, Penang

Author: Quack Moo Meow
Review: This is Penang's take on Texas style BBQ and boy, was it D E L I C I O U S.We had combo A which consisted of pulled pork and ribs. …MoreThis is Penang's take on Texas style BBQ and boy, was it D E L I C I O U S.We had combo A which consisted of pulled pork and ribs.The ribs was incredibly tender and just fell right off the bone. You don't even need a knife to cut through the meat - that was how soft it was. The sauce was a little sweet but not overpowering.The pulled pork was absolutely flavourful, rich and moist.We also had their weekend special, the pork knuckle. It was H U G E.Unlike German pork knuckle, it wasn't crispy but instead it was fatty and tender - which I think is suited to the local taste. Despite looking like it was roasted for a long while, the meat was surprisingly juicy. I would recommend this for probably 3-4 people.It was served with their own version of sauerkraut. Traditional sauerkraut is sour whereas this wasn't. The chef informed us that he wanted to create a taste that locals would enjoy.A worthy mention was their knockout mashed potato. It was smooth and oh-so creamy. Absolutely delicious pairing with all the meats. Had the knuckle been smaller, we would probably ordered more mashed potatoes!!!Also the prices were incredibly fair/affordable for the portion/quality.Again, note that the taste has been designed to cater to the local taste buds - so while it isn't authentic Texas taste, they've definitely used the method of BBQ-ing meat to perfection.Would definitely come again should I visit Penang.
Location: 49-f, Pengkalan Weld, Georgetown, Penang

Author: Alexandra Kabakova
Review: A taste of nyonya flavoring〰️Visited one of Penang’s most established Nyonya kueh-makers since 1933, Moh Teng Pheow.Nyonya Kueh is one of the favourite Peranakan delicacies that have a long …MoreA taste of nyonya flavoring〰️Visited one of Penang’s most established Nyonya kueh-makers since 1933, Moh Teng Pheow.Nyonya Kueh is one of the favourite Peranakan delicacies that have a long history since the 15th Century.  These bite-sized sweets are rich and varied, made from ingredients such as glutinous rice, coconut milk and palm sugar.Peranakan has a very long history in Singapore and Malaysia. They are the descendants of the Straits Chinese that settled along the Malay Archipelago. They have a strong cultural background. These customs and traditions have evolved overtime, having traces of Portuguese, Dutch, British, Malay, Indonesian and Chinese influences. Peranakan cuisines are well liked by the locals in Singapore. These dishes are a combination of both Chinese and Malay food. One of the top hits in Singapore is the Nyonya Kueh. Nyonya is the term for female Peranakans and ‘kuehs’ means cakes, thus Nyonya Kuehs are the cakes made by female Peranakans.〰️ One of my favorite - soft and chewy glutinous rice topped with grated coconut cooked in gula melaka (palm sugar), wrapped with banana leaf for an added dose of fragrance.

Review: A memorable place where once you sat for an hour waiting patiently for Hon Kei pork porridge by the two young men in white pagoda T-shirts slowly cooking one bowl at a time at this junction of Kampung Malabar with Penang Road. Armed with …MoreA memorable place where once you sat for an hour waiting patiently for Hon Kei pork porridge by the two young men in white pagoda T-shirts slowly cooking one bowl at a time at this junction of Kampung Malabar with Penang Road. Armed with fame and fortune from years of sweat and pig entrails, the delicacy is now served in two shophouses down the street. In its place, this kopitiam maintains its draw with Penang lor bak and Char Koay Teow. The lor bak serves shrimp fritters from RM1.80 per biscuit with prices escalating quickly with other deep fried tofu concoctions. Char koay teow is offered without cockles but large prawns are on offer for a price. The kopitiam has a compulsory drink for seat policy and takes full advantage of unsuspecting tourists with a ridiculous RM2.20 for iced kopi, a premium of 40 sen for added tapwater ice.

Wide variety of local food available - the ubiquitous Penang fried koay teow, Rice Rolls with choice of shrimp or charsiew, freshly steamed on the spot, and a rather interesting stall selling deep-fried prawn-paste chicken SKIN (one portion RM5)  There is also an Apom stall (Indian pancake, made to order, 5 for RM3)  Alas, the or-chien (Oyster Omelette) was a huge disappointment - miserable-looking oysters and in miniscule amount, more tapioca flour paste than egg. Author: Sigita Paliukaitė
Review: A little gem tucked away in the alley just off Chulia street. A place equally appreciated by locals and by travellers. A place equally appreciated by locals and by travellers. But you have to be either lucky to stumble across it accidentally or to be told about it by someone who's already been lucky to discover it. Perhaps that only adds charm to it..The food is amazing- simple as that. It's hearty home made Malay dishes, following the recipes cooked at home by generations of the owner’s family. Made from scratch. I've seen them grinding their own spices! No other place you can try fish curry with baby shark, their laksa is the best in town (and I do take the ownership of this statement because I've tried laksa in about 5 other places around Georgetown) and my vegan friends raved about their veggie curry for days!All food is halal.Why they're are not on any guides, with only a modest amount of reviews on the web?- because they're fresh and new!Prices are very reasonable to low, considering the quality of food. The place itself- it's chill, charming, inspiring. And if you're really lucky, you might have dinner there at a time of live music- have you ever heard Malay folk songs played by guitar and a flute?..I honestly have never left such a long review. But this place must be shared and appreciated. So do yourself a favour and add the brick cafe to your list of places to go to.

Author: Adrian Cheah
Review: Traditional and avant-garde Asian cuisine at Maple PalaceWhen my classmates from Han Chiang High School decided to have a mini class …MoreTraditional and avant-garde Asian cuisine at Maple PalaceWhen my classmates from Han Chiang High School decided to have a mini class reunion, Maple Palace was our top choice. The restaurant serves mouth-watering cuisine that is both traditional and avant garde at the same time. It also offers festive Chinese New Year dishes synonymous with good luck and prosperity. On top of that, the quality of the delicacies at Maple Palace has been consistent throughout my visits in the past.We started our dinner with Yee Sang, one dish where everyone joins in the fun to Lo Hei. We tossed the salad as high as we could using chopsticks while shouting out good stuff in Hokkien of what we hoped would happen in the coming year – "Heng ah! Ong ah! Huat ah!". It is call for our lives to flourish, to prosper and for our dreams to develop into reality. After such a rambunctious start, we were in for a real treat. Next was a truly unique four seasons creation of exquisite cuisine. Artistically presented, it is a visual feast as much as a gastronomic delight. Hanging on a Chinese brush rack was a string of crispy chicken wings stuffed with Tobiko (flying fish roe). In small little glasses below, skewed pan-fried scallops with red and green peppers coated with a dark savour sauce. On white little saucers lay golden breaded prawns. And on a platter was spread Spanish Iberico Char Siew Salad with lotus root chips. It looked so beautiful. The cameras certainly had their full share of the dish before we dug in, doing justice to today's dining prelusory experience of photographing one’s dinner treat.Being the Chinese New Year season, we next had the popular assorted preserved waxed meat claypot rice (Lap Mei Fun). This dish had different types of waxed meat including Chinese pork sausage and Chinese duck or goose liver sausage. I am glad that the chef served a plate of greens on the side to balance out the high fat content of this item. The next dish was simply delicious. Braised broccoli topped with scrambled egg white and crabmeat. It was such a lovely combination and we enjoyed this dish very much. This roast chicken dish was served with crispy salmon skin flavoured with salted duck egg yolk. It was a welcome surprise compared to the mundane roast chicken topped with prawn crackers. The chicken was tender and its skin crispy. Buddha's delight, often transliterated as Luo Han Chai is another popular dish during Chinese New Year. This authentic recipe has eighteen key ingredients which many find it is too tedious to get all the ingredients, and therefore omit some components without sacrificing the flavour. The chef at Maple Palace had done the same while creatively encircling the vegetarian dish with a yam ring, making it a more hearty dish. The flavours were still recognisable although he added broccoli and snow fungus to the mix.Osmanthus and wolfberry jelly is a wonderful way to conclude a satisfying meal. Each serving consists of eight ingot-shaped jelly with a longan in the centre of each. It was so good that we just had to order another portion. To the Chinese, an ingot (is a form of ancient Chinese currency) is symbolic of prosperity and wealth due to their auspicious shape.We were happy with the service at Maple Palace. It was additionally comforting as the waiters were attentive and responded quickly to requests. After every dish, they would came around to change the plates so that we could enjoy each dish without the sight of lingering sauces from the previous dish. With good food and service, it is no wonder that Maple Palace is popular among locals.
Location: 47, Jln Sultan Ahmad Shah, Georgetown, George Town, Penang
