Author: Jake Lee
Review: Being a Penangite myself, currently residing in UK, the Maple Palace venue after various morphing, have always been a local popular reliable eatery, frequented by locals and internationals. Slightly pricey, but well mitigated by it's superb …MoreBeing a Penangite myself, currently residing in UK, the Maple Palace venue after various morphing, have always been a local popular reliable eatery, frequented by locals and internationals. Slightly pricey, but well mitigated by it's superb environment but primarily, reliably delicious food.Naturally, I had a dinner for my relatives during my recent visit to my hometown, which in this occasion sadly accumulated into a rather negative experience.We called into the restaurant and discussed our menu choice with the captain where we categorically requested for a normal sit down dinner format whereupon all the various dishes are brought out together for a hearty family type dinner environment.However, on the night of the dinner, the various dishes were brought out erratically, basically one at a time with approximately 10 minutes intermission between them akin to a banquet style dinner where each dish cooked in size to equate to total number of diners is appropriately brought out simultaneously.Naturally in this occasion, it is totally embarrassing to have a tiny dish placed in the centre of a large round table for 8 diners! Furthermore, by the time the other dishes arrived, the other dishes are cold. Worse still, no rice was offered and when they arrived, they were also rendered cold waiting for the dishes to slowly make their way to our table.My only saving grace rests on the fact that all my diners were close relatives and the typical family banter aided to smooth the point blank chaos of the dining experience!However, the final disappointment emerged when I tried to pay with my credit card which was declined. I then tried to pay with my bank debit card which was also declined! Luckily for me, I had just exchanged some sterling pounds to local currency and had enough to pay off this hugh bill.Naturally, the refusal of both my credit and debit card rested on my mind the whole evening, have my accounts been hacked, fraud, etc? I know there is certainly more than enough funds and credit in both my accounts.The next morning, I immediately rushed to the nearest ATM and tested both cards, and both cards worked perfectly! I was then advised by a local friend that certain commercial establishments practice this "refusal" to accept credit card payments in favour for cash!Naturally I am in no position to verify the latest allegation, however, in conclusion, that dinner experience was certainly not enjoyable, most stressful right from the start as I endeavour to be a polite host and the fact that both my credit and debit cards are refused, considering one came from a bank, the other from a  building society, both reputable sterling financial establishments in Europe, all accounts for my award of a single star in this review for this otherwise magnificent establishment.I am sadly dismayed that slowly but surely one by one of Penang's iconic eateries are taking their clientele for granted by letting their standards deteriorate.
Location: 47, Jln Sultan Ahmad Shah, Georgetown, George Town, Penang

Review: Having not tasted the Duck Kway Chap for nearly six years, I was surprised by how long the queue of patrons and tourists was from the stall. Was this phenomenon the outcome of Mark Weins's review on youtube? I decided to come early the next …MoreHaving not tasted the Duck Kway Chap for nearly six years, I was surprised by how long the queue of patrons and tourists was from the stall. Was this phenomenon the outcome of Mark Weins's review on youtube? I decided to come early the next day, and was thrilled to be only the third one in line.  The assorted display of meats, duck and pig heads, coagulated blood cubes, as well as intestines was a sight to behold, making my stomach churn with hunger.  I ordered the 'Jia Liao' version, or the one with a  bigger portion, costing a mere RM10.00.  I was glad that the stall operaters still maintained their generosity with toppings, which seemed like a miniature hill atop the square rice noodles.  Every slurp and bite was a burst of flavour and my, I could not describe how rich the broth was. The ground chilies, with tiny bits of lime rind, were equally memorable, adding a delightful citrusy and piquant flavour to the noodles.  The duck meat was smoky and tender, well-infused with herbs and soy sauce. The coagulated blood melted right in my mouth, no chewing needed.  On the other hand, the intestines, well-cleaned and odourless, providing a good bite. To add more linings to my praise, the slivers of pig ears, with soft edible cartilages, were crisp and gelatinous, whetting my appetite. My top favourite being the rice noodles, which had improved so much in texture over the past six years, so smooth and springy to say the least, not easily turning mushy in the hot, rich broth, lifting the Kway Chap to a whole new level - amazing!

Review: The char kuey teow here is delicious, patronised this place back-to-back two days in a row. Each plate of char kuey teow is made to order …MoreThe char kuey teow here is delicious, patronised this place back-to-back two days in a row. Run by a Chinese family and cooked by a father and son duo, they put lard bits when cooking the dish. Each plate of char kuey teow is made to order at the front of the shop, so expect to have to queue an hour or so for a plate. There are 2 sizes; 'Small' for those who are health conscious but still want a little taste and 'Big' for the regular person. If not mistaken the pricing was RM 6 and RM 8 respectively. They also serve herbal drinks which is also known as 'leong cha', chinese tea, soft drinks and fresh fruit juice. Pricing ranged from rm2-5 I believe.The lady who's in-charge of taking orders of the drinks has a limited English vocabulary, so I would like to ask tourists and fellow Asians who can't speak any of the Chinese dialects like Hokkien, Cantonese and Mandarin to be more understanding. It's not that she's rude because business is booming, it's because she's frustrated that some tourists and locals don't listen. Please queue up in an orderly manner, don't cut queue, and stand at a safe distance away from the wok for your own safety.The family who runs the place tries their best to accommodate everyone and usually will open big parasols to provide shade for the customers but this place is overcrowded on most days because of how small the shop is so be prepared to share a table with strangers. There is no AC so it's going to be very warm and humid in the restaurant. Please dress lightly and respectfully.

Vans often arrive (from Thailand?) laden with inebriating delights and the staff hurry to shunt everything inside. They're not quite …MoreBy some mysterious voodoo powers, this place is far cheaper than almost any other booze shop in Malaysia. Vans often arrive (from Thailand?) laden with inebriating delights and the staff hurry to shunt everything inside. They're not quite so attentive towards customers - seemingly quite happy to let you figure everything out. Grab your own drinks, pay at the counter, go outside, find your own table and chair (in the cubby-hole to the right of the shop) and get yourself sat down. It's all very laissez-faire.This is a good place to get chatting to people. Unfortunately, if you stay for a couple of hours, you will almost certainly encounter a 'friend' who will want money or will generally become a pest.SPECIAL PRO-TIP! There is actually an EVEN CHEAPER place just a few doors down to the left of the shop. It will look closed, but if you rattle the gates, a man will emerge who can sell you all kinds of marvels. You can't sit out there during the daytime.

Review: It has been two long years since we have been able to come to experience Penang's  delicious food and history. One of our goals is always to savour its authentic Nyonya / Peranakan cuisine which is really difficult to find other than in …MoreIt has been two long years since we have been able to come to experience Penang's  delicious food and history. One of our goals is always to savour its authentic Nyonya / Peranakan cuisine which is really difficult to find other than in Penang or Malacca... cooked well of course! 🤣After seeing all the positive reviews, we were crazy excited about dining at Winn's Cafe and considered ourselves extremely lucky to be able to get a reservation on short notice especially on Valentine's Day! Let me tell you, they did not disappoint and in fact, EXCEEDED all of our high expectations with their exceptional food and even greater customer service making for an UNFORGETTABLE dining experience!As this was our first time, we asked for recommendations and the friendly staff suggested some incredible dishes and just the right amount to fill you up without being too full. Throughout the meal, we had the manager and even the owner Winnie come out to wish us happy Valentines Day and see how our meal was coming along. We took the opportunity to chat, all culinary questions and give our compliments to the chef for an amazing meal. The owner, seeing how much we were savoring every last bite, genterously sent over complimentary dessert(s) so we had 3 to enjoy!!But the experience was not over even after we paid the bill! On her suggestion, we went outside to look at the organic herb garden and the owner and manager took time to come outside to give us a private tour pointing out all of the different herbs that go into their food! This was truly an exceptional, unique and UNFORGETTABLE dining experience. We look forward to coming back again and would highly encourage everybody to try their delicious food! The hype is real!
Location: 2, Jalan Irrawaddi, George Town, Penang

Review: Best Nonya food I've had.My fave is the nasi ulam, which is a blend of raw herbs and spices chopped so …MoreBest Nonya food I've had.My fave is the nasi ulam, which is a blend of raw herbs and spices chopped so finely that is meant to be mixed with the rice it comes with, and has a unique flavor that's is strong yet, because of the fineness of the chopped herbs, it still gives me a sense that is delicate.  And it is not cooked with oil, my mom always says she can eat many many bowls of this without ever getting full (it's a good thing).  My recommendation, don't add the sambal or the lime that's provided to avoid ruining the taste.In a close second place is the kerabu kacang botol.  I've had kacang botol at other places, and somehow, they just don't measure up.  Other places either leave the kacang botol with strong grassy taste (but to be fair, that wasn't a kerabu so maybe the grassy taste couldn't be covered up), or just doesn't taste as good.  Winn's kerabu kacang botol has just the right balance of sweet, sour and spicy, with a touch of "laksa" flavor.I also love the curry chicken, and perut ikan (the soup reminds me of Penang laksa).Many times I've gone with my parents and their friends, and after we order and finish one round of dishes (which usually would be enough for them at other places), we ordered a second round of dishes.  That's how good Winn's is.

Review: Alot of hit and miss. The service was great, but the salesman was very pushy. The rating must be made known to the management therefore a gentle 2 stars. …MoreAlot of hit and miss. The service was great, but the salesman was very pushy. The rating must be made known to the management therefore a gentle 2 stars.Basically  salesperson kept pushing to order live seafood. Ordered 2 crabs and tomyum prawn, then was asked if i wanna add on live big head prawns etc. I think experience of the customers are important, and a well balanced dishes will satisfy one, instead of keep wanting to nail down bigger orders.I was told mantis prawn to be around 250g per piece, ordered 2. Then I saw a promotion item, cheese baked frozen large mantis prawn, rm38 each. Wanted to cancel the live one and go for the cheese baked one, then I was told that those frozen mantis prawns has got some smell, dont recommend it. Why put up for promotion if the food is not up to standard?  Then end up in excess of 350g per piece, so RM241 for 2 mantis prawn. It tastes alright, but does not match the price la to be honest.Here comes the local live crabs, claw with muscle atrophy, no meat. Fedback with 10% discount.So what was good? All the cheaper food like tomyum prawn(very good), teochew noodles(good), and eggs with bittergourd(excellent) were good. Kamheong lala were not fresh.We came around 10pm, it was the last table(was told that shop is open anyway). So it sums up our family (group of 5) experience there, with RM588.Basically, cheap food are good, but stay away from pushy sale as it does not stay with the hype. Business can only sustain with feedback like that taken into account.

Review: While travelling, I've come across many a burger joint but surprisingly, none like two buns (at least not in asia).  Yes, there are many quant cafes that try to push the sales of burgers and even popularise the diner theme in South East …MoreWhile travelling, I've come across many a burger joint but surprisingly, none like two buns (at least not in asia).  Yes, there are many quant cafes that try to push the sales of burgers and even popularise the diner theme in South East Asia. In this case, these guys have taken a slightly retro theme and moedrnised it.A simple yet presentable menu, accompanied by good service and some helpful recommendations made me feel at ease. I didn't have some hyped up expectation in mind because at the end of the day I don't feel as though many people understand how to create a stand-out patty in the asian market.  What I'm trying to say is that not many restraunts that offer a "mouth-watering" or "talk of the town" kind of burger actually get it right.Two Buns is you average cosy shop, with a great little selection of burgers, some pretty rich shakes and a retro King of Fighters arcade console to boot. The selection of music is quited chilled as well and the overall vibe or feng shui is brilliant.I quite enjoyed the Cookies and Cream shake and the Beefy Business burger. The shake was a decent size and was definitely one of the better shakes I have had in Malaysia. The burger followed soon after and it too was a pleasant surprise. Yes the burgers here aren't huge but if you visit any international burger shop coming up in the world now, smaller portions are a trend.  Whilst sacrificing a bit of size these places focus more on the quality of their product and presentation. At the end of the day, how critical are you going to be when it comes to the presentation of a burger people?!The burger was great, and most importantly the patty was fresh. The meat used in the patty is obviously of a decent standard and it was very well seasoned. The sauce was nice and the addition of peanut butter in my burger was also very interesting.  Nothing really took away from the burger and I felt as though it was quite a solid meal.  Again, I understand that it is not the cheapest place in town, but I am a person who eats a burger as a treat maybe once every two months.So if you are looking to spend under 10 ringgit and eat lunch here every day, this probably isn't your jam! But if you wish to enjoy a well made burger in the heart of George Town, Penang, then there isn't a better place.  I'm not just saying this because of the burger, it's the ambience, the feel, the drinks, and yes....THERES ALCOHOL!BOTTOM LINE -  If you're in the mood for a good burger and a reason to chill out, you gotta check this place out.

Review: If you are just having kuih on vacation, this won't take such a big bite out of your travel budget. It is located walking distance behind the Rich Wives market of Pulau Tikus, opposite the police station. Double portions of Nyonya kuih are …MoreIf you are just having kuih on vacation, this won't take such a big bite out of your travel budget. It is located walking distance behind the Rich Wives market of Pulau Tikus, opposite the police station. Double portions of Nyonya kuih are RM2.50 per pack, not dissimilar in price to KL's Nyonya Colours but substantially better tasting from freshly baked ingredients. At RM1.25 a piece, it's size was double that of Chulia Street Moh Teng Pheow factory outlet offering. Recipe made a difference to its rendition of Kuih Bengka Ubi (tapioca) with more desiccated coconut in its starchy chew, rather different from the kuih my mum once bought from Chowrasta market. Buy a pack of 5 assorted for RM6. Also offered are experimental multi-coloured Mochi with various fillings for the sweet-toothed, a recipe far from the oishii Japanese delicacy, only for diabetics with hara-kiri on their minds. While it is common sense to be pork free for Nyonya kuih making, today's promoter was plugging the siew bao.Pork free siew bao just does not make any Charsiew sense and it's a slippery slope to compete with Hong Kong's Char Chan Teng menu. Stick to what Nyonya knows best with pulut, sago, tapioca and Gula Melaka please...

Author: Dr Albert Chan
Review: We visited the Mermaid Cafe in August 2018 and thoroughly enjoyed the dining experience. The Boxing Chicken (deep-fried chicken wing cutlets perfectly seasoned with salt and pepper) started things off - it was easily one of the best fried …MoreWe visited the Mermaid Cafe in August 2018 and thoroughly enjoyed the dining experience. The Boxing Chicken (deep-fried chicken wing cutlets perfectly seasoned with salt and pepper) started things off - it was easily one of the best fried chicken wing dishes I'd ever sampled! The Mermaid's Signature Soup (fresh mint leaves, fish ball and egg drop) was also pretty good - served steaming hot (just the way I like it!).For the mains, there was a wide variety of fish on offer - stingray, grouper, mackerel, pomfret, salmon, red snapper, threadfin and jade perch - and one had a choice of 3 sauces to accompany the fish - signature sambal chilli paste, garlic butter and homemade pesto. For us, the standout combination here was the stingray and signature sambal chilli paste - gloriously flavoursome and comfortably one of the best spicy fish dishes I'd ever tasted!I had no problem with the slightly limited choice of desserts because the very tasty and refreshing Fruity Lemon Grass Jelly (fresh lemon grass, grass jelly, rock sugar and mixed fruits) perfectly concluded our meal.The owners Alex Tan and his wife Shiau Chean were on hand to provide expert guidance on the menu choices and excellent customer service. The restaurant was extremely clean and featured an attractive and comfortable decor. I thoroughly recommend the Mermaid Cafe to all Penangites and tourists.
Location: 86 B&C, Lorong Macalister, George Town, Penang

Author: Shanarai
Review: Truth be told, I called the restaurant to make a reservation 2 months prior to our special day but 3 weeks later, I followed up with the restaurant through whatsapp as a precaution and I was told by a staff that my reservation was not being …MoreTruth be told, I called the restaurant to make a reservation 2 months prior to our special day but 3 weeks later, I followed up with the restaurant through whatsapp as a precaution and I was told by a staff that my reservation was not being recorded so thank god I played safe and handled the problem. Afterwards, a staff asked us through whatsapp to order our preferred dishes beforehand as well as listing out our special requirements in order to ensure a smooth service on the eventual day which is understandable. For some reason, we had to repeat our food order twice but it is a minor hiccup.We came for our anniversary during Christmas Day hence some new main dishes(1 fish, 1 lamb, 2 beef, 1 lobster) with a limited time Christmas menu. For me, it would be better to give us 1-2 more fish choices (chicken and duck wouldn’t fit the high-end price obviously) for those who aren’t a fan of beef, lamb and are terrified of the lobster price.The place has a romantic feel at night accompanied by soft music which suits its ambience. Customers are mostly considerate here so we enjoyed our food in a quiet soothing manner.The toilet here was clean and spacious for those who want to accompany their child or elderly in. The downside is that only one person can use it at a time so it is important to be patient.Our food was delicious from start to finish (favourites being scallops, oysters, pumpkin soup and chef’s special) and it was good to end the night with a special anniversary surprise courtesy of the restaurant. For normal people like us who do not have the luxury of trying fine dining on a regular basis, this is perfect enough for us.Price-wise, there is a 10% service charge but it is certainly worth the experience for regulars and first timers.I have to say that the service was near impeccable during our time here. The staffs were friendly and quick to re-fill our drinks, not to mention quite attentive on the food feedback. Some suggestions I could give would be for the staffs to tell us which dining utensils to use for which dish because not every customer is an expert on fine dining. Also, it would be best to explain a dish upon serving rather than having someone come over and explaining later when the customers have started eating.Overall, we had a wonderful time here and would gladly consider coming again in the future.

Author: David Chew
Review: When in Penang, a visit to this place is a must, as it houses probably the best Lor Bak ever. There are other stalls in this place selling wantan mee, char koay teow, chicken rice, porridge, hokkien mee and also not forgetting Annie's Nasi …MoreWhen in Penang, a visit to this place is a must, as it houses probably the best Lor Bak ever. There are other stalls in this place selling wantan mee, char koay teow, chicken rice, porridge, hokkien mee and also not forgetting Annie's Nasi Lemak (a must try as well).Parking is normally along Aboo Sittee Lane, but that can be a bit of an issue if you're close to peak hours. You may want to park a little further away and walk to Kheng Pin instead.I have been to this place for about 40 years now, and the food there, though some stalls have changed through the years, has never failed me. It's quite astonishing that almost every single stall serves really good food - a rarity. But most come here for the lor bak, as it's another one of Penang's long standing institutions.

Author: Adrian Cheah
Review: Elegance of Japanese cuisine at MirakuWhen dining at Miraku you would be able encounter such an art form as soon as …MoreElegance of Japanese cuisine at MirakuWhen dining at Miraku you would be able encounter such an art form as soon as you are served, so much so that you are compelled to feast with your eyes first. Here, food preparation is such a delicate craft that it is pursued with passion and executed to perfect artistry. Miraku offers more than just sushi and sashimi and ramen. There is a wide variety of Japanese delights to choose from. Before you place your order, ask the captain about their seasonal offerings. Miraku has some flown in directly from Japan.During a recent visit to the restaurant we were served Miraku Salad with salmon, crab meat, octopus and scallop with a selection of dressings. I would usually opt for the sesame dressing which harmonises well the flavours of fresh seafood and crispy iceberg lettuce. Also remember to add succulent grilled oysters with spicy miso paste to your list of items to try at Miraku. Miraku's Dragon Roll – deep-fried prawn roll sushi wrapped with avocado and topped with tobiko is among my favourites. If you are seated at the main atrium where the chef would be preparing this dish right before you, you would be amazed with his meticulous attention to detail. Spider Roll – deep-fried soft shell crab sushi with cucumber and mayonnaise was another wonderful dish we tried.Once at Miraku we had fresh hotate (Hokkaido scallops) and it was a real treat. The fresh scallops sashimi was sweet in taste and soft in texture with rich decadence – a tasty realm of seafood luxury. Because of the need for freshness of the seafood, I would usually go for seasonal items from Japan that are available. Although they are not on the main menus, the captain would be happy to run down the list. The lobster above was glazed with miso butter and grilled over a charcoal stove. The smoky flavour that accentuated the sweetness of the lobster meat made it such a scrumptious delight. Flying fish (Tobiuo in Japanese) is a seasonal fish in Japan from Spring to Summer. This was my first time sampling this fish and it was simply fantastic! I feel lucky that although living in Penang, we were able to savour bountiful catch from the seas of Japan.If after all the sashimi, sushi and grilled items you still have room for more, try the garlic fried rice or Niku Udon – thick white wheat noodles cooked in hot fish soup with thinly sliced beef. A bowl of clams in clear broth would accompany the fried rice perfectly. Tempura style deep-fried Vanilla ice cream top with read beans is excellent to conclude a satisfying gastronomical experience. If you are lost and spoilt for choice, and do not know where to start ordering, it is a safe bet to try one of their set menus. It has a combination of various items for you to indulge.
Location: 2, Lebuhraya Maktab, George Town, Penang

Author: David Chew
Review: Due to the variety of food available here, many locals and visitors to the island throng to this place, as it's a convenient, one stop shop for all the Penang delicacies. Housed along in the corner lot of a row of old heritage building …MoreDue to the variety of food available here, many locals and visitors to the island throng to this place, as it's a convenient, one stop shop for all the Penang delicacies. Housed along in the corner lot of a row of old heritage building houses, this hawker centre now boasts of almost 25 different stalls selling everything from Satay to Hokkien mee to even Western food as well.Parking is a nightmare here on Presgrave Street, and be prepared to walk a bit in order to get here. You may even need to park as far away as Presgrave Street Ghaut, about 200m away. However, if you're early enough or stay away from peak dining hours, you might just get lucky.The food quality here is generally good. All the dishes I've sampled here are good examples of what Penang has to offer. Oh, do try the pork or mutton satay from the stall along the street that's manned by and old uncle and auntie. It's a delicacy nowadays to be able to get satay with this sort of meat.Also outside is a stall that sells nostalgia, as far as I am concerned. This roti bakkua fare is so rare, and being able to chow down on it always brings a smile to my face.All-in-all, it's a good place to pop by for a meal.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Review: A famous street of hawkers slowly moves off street into the courtyards of the houses. Mediocre has nowhere to go but stay here. Mediocre has nowhere to go but stay here. The much talked about Hokkien Mee (RM6) is served in a spicy but weak prawn bisque, mainly due to the lack of pork bone, as she was busy shredding up stale roast pork for garnishings. The much loved cendol (RM4.50) while maintaining the sweetness of the palm sugar in santan use an artificial coloured green grass jelly, disappointedly not made from sago flour and mung beans. The Char Koay Teow uncle sits forlorn and disinterested, reminiscing of better days of yesteryear, while his feisty daughter fries up a plate with gusto, perhaps now finally taking on the main attraction for RM6. The main attraction in the evening will surely be the gooey fried oyster omelette (RM11) or an eggless Char Koay Kak or fried turnip cake(RM4) for a late supper.

Author: Ben Yap
Review: Normal hawker fare and western dishes like chicken chop and fries. Difficult to accommodate more than 4 people per table as per SOP requirements. Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Ooi Gareth

Author: Siew Ling Lau
Review: One of the best fried chicken skins I have ever eaten.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: ming wee Koh

Tried the charcoal fried kuey teow which i find it on an okay level. But definitely a great place for dinner. Shop hours are until 10pm though, where they would close shop rather quickly after.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Adrian Sia
Review: Curry mee, CKT, Fried Oyster,  888 Hokkien mee recommended to try here
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Delyn デリン
Review: We found a roadside parking and walked to the hawker center. We ordered the famous 3888 fried oysters and “hokkien mee” (prawn noodle) and also “chendul” (green pandan rice flour jelly, coconut milk, palm sweet sugar syrup, shaved ice) Overall taste is awesome, however we hoped that the hawker center hygiene can be further improved
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Mandy Marston
Review: The main food over here is the 888 Hokkien Mee!!! Please order that when you’re here if not you will seriously regret, 10/10. ABC with ice cream is also superb, 10/10. Wan thun mee is quite good too, 8/10. Oyster and Loh Bak are so so for me, 5/10 for both.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: KH Fong
Review: The food here taste good.It’s really street food.It’s right behind The Wembley Hotel. …MoreThe food here taste good.It’s really street food.It’s right behind The Wembley Hotel.888 Hokkien prawn noodles is tasty.Char Kway Tiao is better than the one at Siam road.Chendol is very good.Price is reasonable.Must come and try.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Sean Sim
Review: Pretty good hawker food. The Penang chee cheong fun was very nice. The curry mee was ok, wished there was more condiments. The sar hor fun was so-so. Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Wong Francis
Review: Some very good food,  such as possibly the one and only place where u can find pork satay. Other offerings are the usual standard ones like Hokkien fried kway diao,  cendol etc. Authentic dining experience which makes Penang famous,  reasonably priced but expect no aircon and not so comfortable seating.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Khor Yong Kean
Review: This little house converted food court is famous for fried oyster, hokkien mee and ice kacang. The stall by the roadside outside the food court selling wan tan mee is also nice. It is worth the visit if you are nearby here. It is not far …MoreThis little house converted food court is famous for fried oyster, hokkien mee and ice kacang. The stall by the roadside outside the food court selling wan tan mee is also nice. It is worth the visit if you are nearby here. It is not far from 1st Avenue and Komtar, and walkable distance from some nearby hotels like Neo, The Wembley-St Giles and Jens hotel.*Visited in Dec 2020
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Peiyi Deng
Review: Great little local place with some seats sheltered from the rain. Cendol was so amazing, I would say better than the Teochew cendol on Penang street. Prawn noodles were good too and you can add more stuff for an extra charge. Satay was so-so and cold considering that it should be hot off the grill.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Mei Lin Lim
Review: Beware on the lady who sells the fried chicken. Upon noticing that I’m not local said the price today is rm4 instead of the stated rm3.80. So dishonest.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Richard Smittenaar
Review: A lot of worthwhile options here. We enjoyed everything we ordered, except for the curry cheun fung, with our favourites being the curry mee, the stir fried turnip cakes from the stall across the road, and the char koay teow.  And still plenty more good stuff to come back for.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Min Tze Khor
Review: Came and try their duck egg char koay teow. Dine in. And apparently they will charge you if you didn't order any drinks although I ordered the food over there. Is this the norm here in Penang? Duck egg char koay teow tasted different but not to the point of must try.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Dean Southall
Review: Quite close to the Komtar bus station/shopping centre.  I came here on a Saturday night and it was very busy.  I didn't have too much trouble finding a seat but a few people asked to join the table (in a nice manner).  I'd had plenty of …MoreQuite close to the Komtar bus station/shopping centre.  I came here on a Saturday night and it was very busy.  I didn't have too much trouble finding a seat but a few people asked to join the table (in a nice manner).  I'd had plenty of Asian food so I fancied some western food and I noticed on a couple of photos that there's a western stall.  I went to the stall and ordered fish and chips for 10 Rm.  The food arrived at the table and I paid the 10 Rm.  A girl from the drinks stall asked if I wanted to buy a drink.  They didn't have a stout so I politely declined.  The fish and chips were fine for the Rm 10.  I'd come here again.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Tiffany Christina Tran

Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Chien Chai Lye
Review: Busy and popular hawker or street food place in downtown Georgetown.Famous here are 888 Hokkien Prawn Mee, wonton mee, satay, oyster omelette and chendol.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Edward Koo
Review: A street hawker style variety food stalls at a corner unit shop. Fried oyster, char kuey teow, curry noodles, satays are quite good. Portions are slightly smaller than some other food hawker stalls. Cleanliness need to be look into.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Jessy Wong
Review: Speaking as a true Penangite, this is one of the well-loved local food center to dine in Penang! Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Declan Cael
Review: Unfortunately the food that was ordered was not up to standards. Or Chien was tasteless and bland, popiah was soggy, mee jawa lacked flavour, and the ice lemon tea came in cans. Overall a very disappointing experience in comparison to other places in Penang.

Author: rachel lee yew hui

Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Amadeus Low (勇瑜)

Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: 5525 Gunner
Review: The two truly outstanding stalls here are the Curry Mee and Hokkien Mee. I would rate both of them in the top 3 of their respective category in the whole of Penang Island. The other stalls are decent and so that is quite an array of variety for any hawker food lovers.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: David Oon
Review: A new find from Foursquare when I was around Wembley St Giles. Do give the …MoreA new find from Foursquare when I was around Wembley St Giles. Author: Rainy Zhang
Review: Love the noodle here, I had all kinds of toppings to try and feel more than satisfied. The soup is cooked for hours and very very tasty! I will definitely come again and again and again!

Author: Anne Hui Ni

Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Jack Oni

Author: Simon Teh
Review: The 888 hokkein mee is delicious. I ordered one with additional siow bak and hoon chiang for only RM7.50, ready to expect self service and long queue. The hei cheen next door of the 888 hokkein is yummy too. The careful the one by the road side is not as good as the one I suggest.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: JK Thum (TJK)
Review: Very very good street food. Be prepared to wait though. CKT and the 888 Har Mee 2 doors away is the best. Har mee has long long queue.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Steven Saw
Review: The dish of local authenticity, of which the soup is a combination of curry and coconut milk, is always a popular choice for a quick, hearty meal.  A bowl of curry mee typically consists of yellow noodles and rice vermicelli with the …MoreThe dish of local authenticity, of which the soup is a combination of curry and coconut milk, is always a popular choice for a quick, hearty meal.  A bowl of curry mee typically consists of yellow noodles and rice vermicelli with the addition of fried bean curd, cockles, prawns, cuttlefish, cubes of pig's blood and bean sprouts. When in Penang, it is of course recommended to have a bowl of curry mee to soothe your curious palate. Here are one of the delicious Penang for tasty bowls of curry mee. Definitely I will be back again. Love Penang.

Author: Loon Yew Foong

Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Navein N
Review: Food is only so so - not really worth the drive up if you're not already in Georgetown. Cha kuey Teow and curry mee were mediocre, ie below average. Bakkwa bun was average. The dim sum however, was pretty good especially the fried yam basket.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: JH Kwan
Review: Fantastic Penang signature hawker food. The prawn noodle taste wonderful. Very rich and tasty soup base (forgot to snap a pic). Try add-on their “siew yoke”. It’s crunchy and yummy. As for dessert, you may try the delicious cendol. Long queue and waiting time but definitely worth the trip. A variety of good food available under one roof.

Author: Teng Lynn

Author: Sebastian Koh

Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: pei wen su

Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Stephanie Yamamoto
Review: This stall serves an authentic Penang white curry noodles. Spiciness can be adjust accordingly as the white base coconut milk broth is purely blend with herbs. Author: Miss W
Review: Quite good. Variety choices of food here and most of the food are tasty.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Missie Soh

Author: alexendra toh

Author: KT Tan

Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: HY Lee

Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Michael Bollom
Review: Not a huge selection but tons of hustle and bustle with locals.  I thought the famous Hokien mee was more spice than flavour.  The fried carrot cake was much better.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: junseRn Kok
Review: My first time coming here and I am not disappointed. I had their mee jawa and it was not too bad. The fried koay teow is quite good. Author: Jordan Cave
Review: Me oh my the food here! We had the char kway teow, oyster omelette, wantan mee, popiah, hokkien prawn mee, iced kacang, and chendol. The flavours were simply amazing. Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: Isabelle Alyssa
Review: I absolutely love the Fried fish bee hoon soup here. It is absolutely delicious and soothing for the tummy. The fried oyster and prawn mee is also very good. The prices of these dishes are reasonable and some might consider it cheap too. Definitely recommend this place to other people.
Location: 67D, Lebuh Presgrave, George Town, Penang

Author: mariyam ok
Review: Hawker style stalls selling mixed variety food like fried noodles, pan mee , porridge,wonton mee ,etc. I usually take wanton mee or chicken rice. The pork rib rice is also quite good . It is better to be seated outside than inside the shop.Cooler outside

Author: Cindy Chew

Author: xezw
Review: Just arrived in Penang and did not know what to expect, I was hungry and went to the closest hawker centre I could find. Author: ND T
Review: Smashing Hokkien Mee (Prawn Noodles), O Jian (Oyster Omelette) and Western Food. Satay also very good. We had a great time here. It may come across as somewhat unfriendly but it seems to be a recurring practice here in Penang.

Author: Jay T. Walker

Author: Phoena Sang
Review: Always my choice of street food in Penang. The best oyster pancake (O-chian) in my opinion. The roti bakar with the selection of filling on a cart at the front worth coming back again and again. Always buy this for takeaway supper.

Author: f e l i c i a c

Author: Lian Khoon

Author: yemmi yong

Author: ps loh

Author: Gerry Mcarthur
Review: Some very good stalls here.My favourites are.. Fried oyster and Char koay teow but some other nice dishes too

Author: kamil puczko

Staffs are superb friendly, polite and helpful if you have question about the foods. Wine, liquor and cocktail available here. I'd said quite pricey but the food worth for the price. The butterly pate with toast bread just a perfect match for me. Washroom just clean and dry always.  No slippery issue. The only problem you might face is the car parking. Author: Dorene
Review: Very disappointing experience....At first, I thought it would be a wonderful opportunity for my family to have an authentic nyonya dinner here. We really miss our nyonya grandma's cooking. …MoreVery disappointing experience....At first, I thought it would be a wonderful opportunity for my family to have an authentic nyonya dinner here. We really miss our nyonya grandma's cooking.But, my expectation crashed into a million pieces when I saw the main courses of "asam pedas" fish and black pepper chicken with spring onions were basically pre-heated dishes upon order. The dishes served were not even sufficiently warm. The chef also chose to use "fried" fish fillets and chicken pieces. So, it was very doubtful if the dishes were actually freshly prepared. Although the "asam pedas" fish had the obvious combination of spiciness & sourness but we found it was also very sweet. The lady fingers used were hard and chewy. Sad to say, we had eaten better "asam pedas" fish (with fresh fish fillets instead of fried ones) at "economy" rice stalls and at cheaper prices too.As for the black pepper chicken, it had a strong black pepper flavour but it was oily and salty too.Besides these 2 main dishes, we also ordered "otak-otak". It was another disappointment. First, it came in a bowl. No sign of the traditional banana leave. Not even for garnish. Second, we could hardly taste the "daun kadok"...the signature of nyonya otak-otak. It was merely a creamy coconut milk custard with spices. Again, it was also rather sweet.For appetizer, we ordered "pie tee" cups. The shells were soft...they were not crunchy. I love "pie tee" and I was so sad...Lastly, we had "chendols" for dessert. Well, let's just say, there are better ones out there...As for the service, all the staff seem overworked since they were not smiling...not even the cashier. The dishes were also served in a messy manner.

Don't know how they tally the total but at that point, I wantwd to leave as soon as possible. Having a worker stand in front of your table while you eat, is not that great of an experience. Worse was the cleanliness of the place. It was dirty inside & I almost bolted. However, I wanted to at least try its famous soup dishes. Please don't eat the nasi kandar/campur here, the place where they serve the dishes and curries, looks like it has not been clean for a while. They do not prioritize cleanliness at all. Review: Despite being in their 80s, the famous Lim sisters who sell curry mee in Air Itam are not showing any signs of slowing down, let alone retiring. …MoreDespite being in their 80s, the famous Lim sisters who sell curry mee in Air Itam are not showing any signs of slowing down, let alone retiring.In their little shed, tucked away from the main street where the Air Itam market is located, the two octogenarians are still working tirelessly, as they have been since 1946.A visit on Wednesday (July 5) by The Star found Madam Lim Kooi Lye, 83, seated on a plastic stool, busily churning out bowls of curry mee, with the ingredients all within arm's length, while her elder sister Kooi Heang, 85, sat on a rattan chair as she took orders.Asked about retiring, the elder sister smiled and shook her head, saying without hesitation that "as long as we can do it, we will continue".The sisters, who have never married, have made a name for themselves as a "living heritage" who still serve curry mee cooked over a charcoal stove.Their stalls still use low wooden stools and diners will eat, facing them, with their hands cradling their ceramic bowls.The sisters said they started out by helping their mum with the business when they were young.

Author: Evelyn T
Review: Place is super crowded so make sure to make a reservation before going.Food was delicious! It is probably our favourite place for omurice in Penang for …MorePlace is super crowded so make sure to make a reservation before going.Food was delicious! It is probably our favourite place for omurice in Penang for now. Menu is really extensive so there are a lot of choices to choose from and definitely will have something to fit everyone.Taste of food is not very salty with just enough seasoning, except for the cheese sauce which was the saltiest dish we had among our orders.We had the Bento A set, omurice, ham katsu with cheese sauce, gyoza and grape juice.Let's begin with our favourite dish. The omurice. The fried rice had just enough tangy-ness from ketchup, and had lots of carrots, onions and chicken pieces inside it. The demi glacé sauce didn't really have much flavour that I could distinguish, but it provide just enough moisture to complement the omurice. The egg is definitely the star of this dish, and every mouthful of fried rice accompanied.panied with some egg on top just elevates the whole dish. The egg is just so fragrant (like it was fried in really really hot pan until it had the fragrance and flavour of a deep fried egg) but was still runny. One word, perfect 👌.The bento set consists of unagi, tamagoyaki, korokke, ebi tempura and sashimi as its dishes, accompanied with white rice, miso soup, salad and fruit. Unagi was perfectly fluffy and fatty, which just melts in your mouth. Sashimi slices were unexpectedly super thick that I went "wah, so thick leh", everytime my boyfriend had a slice of it.Ham katsu was probably our least favourite dish among all, not because it is not delicious. It is just the ham and cheese sauce were both very salty individually, and will be better accompanied with rice.The gyoza was not my favourite as well as the filling is predominantly vegetables (cabbage and chives I think) and barely had any meat flavour and texture. That being said, it was the juiciest gyoza I've ever had in Penang. It is just that I prefer a meat filling over one that tastes of vegetable only.Prices are reasonable as well, and portion sizes are definitely not something to worry about. You will definitely leave Aji Noren feeling stuffed.Definitely worth going there to give it a try.
Location: 98-G-35, Prima Tanjung, Jalan Fettes, Kampung Belachan, Tanjung Tokong, Pulau Pinang

Author: Ooi Eng Huat
Review: Small Indian banana leaf shop in little India. The moment i got out of my car, i could smell the aroma of spices wafting through the air. Upon arrival, a man at the front greeted me while making fresh hot dosas and as you walk in you will …MoreSmall Indian banana leaf shop in little India. The moment i got out of my car, i could smell the aroma of spices wafting through the air. Upon arrival, a man at the front greeted me while making fresh hot dosas and as you walk in you will see the selection of curries and dishes. While the selection is not very big, it is very down to earth and deeply flavourful. When you take a seat, a banana leaf will be placed infront of you and hot rice would be pilled on. Followed by a man carrying a set of vegetables on one hand and a variety of curries on the other, and he will scoop whichever dish you want onto the banana leaf. Then another man will come to the table and present you a big metal tray filled with fried chicken and curry puffs. I've also ordered their chicken varuval and it was flavour packed but a bit too dry for my taste. Upon finishing my meal, I could not resist but ask for a second helping to rice, curry and vegetables. It simply was too good to pass up on the refill. If you are wondering, the rice, curry and vegetables are all free flowing as part of the banana leaf set and you can request as much as you want, but the fried chicken, curry puffs and other meat dishes are by order basis and will incurr additional charges. At the end i was stuffed and beaming with happiness. After all, the best indicator of good banana leaf rice is that you leave the place very happy and satisfied.The price is very reasonable as a banana leaf set costs rm6 and the fried chicken costs rm4 for a Maryland. The chicken varuval was rm8 for a regular size dish.

Author: The Vegetarian Voyager
Review: Penang is a culinary Mecca, supposedly. The renowned street food was further down for me, plus I was told there might not be enough vegetarian options for me. …MorePenang is a culinary Mecca, supposedly. The renowned street food was further down for me, plus I was told there might not be enough vegetarian options for me.Being with a child by myself, I wouldn't have hiked down there. So I just cabbed it up from the hotel to here.Malaysia is famous for roti canai. In the US, it is and they usually have a coconut based curry. Little did I know that here, the vegetarian version of the curry is usually dal.  So that was disappointing. But everything else was superb.We got an uttapam, a masala dosa, and a roti 'canai'. The sambar, tomato dal, and chutney were free flow and self serve.I fancied the chutney, as usual, given it was so good.The child was friendly-ly threatened by an overzealous server who was only trying to be nice and help the mother (I) as he noticed the child wasn't eating despite the mother's pleading. Two more times of the server's checking in, and tears streamed down the child's eyes, when I asked the server to cut it off and pretended to be the hero to the child telling him I've taken care of it - him :DThe food is quite cheap in Malaysia, probably cheaper than India. Paid and then walked back to the hotel. Which was less than 30 minutes, with the child. Strangely enough, the concierge there told me it would take me over an hour to walk it.More photos and details on my blog - thevegetarianvoyager[dot]com

As for this restaurant, I highly recommend it. Why? There many reasons for that. The first one is of course the taste. For me this might not be the most delicious of the island but it is still pretty good with lots of choices ranging from the usually chicken, beef or even seafood such as squids and prawns which they cooked in different style. It's all around delicious with reasonable price. The most important to me I think is that this place is not crowded. Tourist and people tend to go to the famous restaurant that requires you to queue for a long time. Why waste time as this one is almost taste the same with big names of nasi kandar restaurants around here and even cheaper compare to some . Review: Located at the junction of Union Street and Penang Street, this nasi kandar institution has satisfied generations of Penangites and visitors from around the world as well. There's a very good reason for that.Parking in this area is almost impossible to find during weekdays as it's located smack in the middle of the business district of Penang. However, the shop opens at 7am and you could make it your breakfast spot and be assured of parking. If you're a tourist and get around on foot, it'll be easier for you to get here.And yet, when you arrive, you'll probably find a queue of patrons lining up while the server skilfully scoops your choices into a plate for consumption. The choices of different curries are aplenty, but one item which everyone goes for is - the fried chicken.I had lunch with a friend and we ordered dishes on separate plates instead. The food is good - curries are aromatic and are just right to whet your appetite. Some other nasi kandar shops feature curries that are sometimes too intense.The shop has ample seating inside and also on the five-foot way as well. If you see a middle-aged man with greying hair on his sides behind the counter, say hi to him (Ali), a most friendly guy.As a Penangite myself who grew up on food such as this, nasi kandar Merlin has one of the most authentic tastes that has not changed through the years they have been in existence.Brave the parking, it's worth the effort to savour this must-try venue in Penang.
Location: 1A Union Street Georgetown, George Town, Pulau Pinang

Review: At the corner of Carnarvon Street and Melayu Street, Ping Hooi is quite a popular haunt for breakfast and mid-morning diners. It has a variety of Penang favourites there, and the Tiger Char Koay Teow is located in this brightly coloured …MoreAt the corner of Carnarvon Street and Melayu Street, Ping Hooi is quite a popular haunt for breakfast and mid-morning diners. It has a variety of Penang favourites there, and the Tiger Char Koay Teow is located in this brightly coloured coffee shop.Parking is literally non existent unless you get very lucky and park along Carnarvon or the adjoining roads around it. You might get lucky after a few rounds, so do keep trying your luck.The early morning stalls include Hokkien Mee, Lor Bak, Duck meat beehoon soup and others, and are all very good, with the exception of the lor bak, which , to me, was evident that sugar was a key ingredient in the deep fried offerings.For a coffee shop that's almost 65 years old, it still looks good, and even has the old fashioned booth sitting by the side wall, so retro - but it just lends a charming vibe to the whole place.I also loved the back area of the coffee shop, being so colourful and even has plastic mobiles hanging on it (see video) which was such a hoot!Nice place to come and savour some of Penang's delights and immerse yourself in a really old coffee shop.
Location: 179, Lebuh Carnarvon, Georgetown, George Town, Penang

Author: Louis Downs
Review: We called for reservations and were told that Ah Chui does not take any reservations, just show up and plenty of room.  When we got there several tables were empty. We sat but a waitress told us they were reserved and that she'd find us a …MoreWe called for reservations and were told that Ah Chui does not take any reservations, just show up and plenty of room.  When we got there several tables were empty. We sat but a waitress told us they were reserved and that she'd find us a seat.  She then walked off and we never saw her, so we walked around and found another table that had been empty the whole time. Later she came to our table and took our order.  It was busy and things were slow to come from the kitchen, but when they did come the sting ray was smaller than any other seafood restaurant but for the same price.  The vegetables were without any spice of flavor.  Finally, 1/2 way through the meal the waitress came to tell us that they had run out of sotong.  When my wife complained that we'd put in the order long before the waitress said that you put in your order and it is prioritized.  If they don't run out they will serve you.  Later some came to another table near us.  The shrimp fritters were 1/2 tiny shrimps and 1/2 shells with no shrimps.  And all of the seafoods were obviously the smallest and cheapest the proprietor could buy.  Even though the restaurant served the cheapest it could get, the price was more than we've paid at several of the prime Chinese seafood places on the island.  This was a really disappointing restaurant, and I'd advise anyone who thinks it comes anywhere near the standard of Penang seafood to go to an establishment that does come up to that standard.

This place is literally a legend. To many, this is the BEST Nasi Kandar in the world.If you are in Penang, this is a wholistic experience not to be missed.-You begin with the 20 minute long queue, surrounded by aging shop-lots that epitomise the heritage of Penang. It’s a wait for sure, but the wait makes the meal all the more worth it.-the moment you enter, you are engulfed by rich flavourful smells of curries. The industry shown by the chefs and staff gives you the vibes that these people here are the master of their craft. Even the staff serving the Nasi Kandar dishes exude such confidence, it was hard to not notice.-the assortment of dishes are incredible - from Ayam Kampung Bawang Goreng to Lamb Shanks and even Duck meat, it was a variation I have never seen before in a Nasi Kandar shop. For Vegetarians, fret not. The options here will not disappoint. Tofu, eggs, fried vegetable dishes, bitter gourd, all these are readily available.-despite the prices being higher than average, the portion was INCREDULOUSLY BIG. I was already struggling just to finish my food, and I ultimately skipped dinner because I was way too full.As a Penangnite, this may not be my favourite Nasi Kandar stall (I love Jaafar’s and NS nasi Kandar, which I will feature soon enough). Nevertheless, I would still recommend all to give this place a shot. It’s for the wholistic experience. That experience makes it all worth coming here. You can’t miss it.

Author: Iise Chew
Review: 📍Hudson's Deli, Penang (Non-Halal)🥪Tucked quietly in suburb at Tanjung Bungah is perhaps the BEST-tasting …More📍Hudson's Deli, Penang (Non-Halal)🥪Tucked quietly in suburb at Tanjung Bungah is perhaps the BEST-tasting Sandwich shop I've ever experienced. Christian, the Austrian Executive Chef of 5 star hotels around the world, serves the extreme best of his capabilities. The cuisine screams of a certain class; a mixture of simplicity with the best of imported ingredients, and a strong desire by a head chef to see to the satisfaction in his customers.😋Being opened for the past 2 years, Hudson's Deli has been weathering the COVID-19 storm with success because of the steady stream of customers. From what initially was 50% expatriates and 50% locals, it would appear that the local numbers have overtaken the expatriates, because of what seems to be positive word of mouth reviews.🌍Christian and his wife, Pearl both run the show; they're all smiles and pleasantries. Christian's repertoire is expansive.. He's been an executive chef and even holding the position of general manager in various 5-star hotels around the world - Austria, Hong Kong, Thailand, Australia, Malaysia, China and even the Philippines.🍔Being in Penang with Pearl (who is a Kuchingite), Christian was on a witch-hunt for a satisfactory Reuben Sandwich; it was a futile attempt. This spurred the start of the lovely Hudson's Deli, the name Hudson being inspired by his grandson who was born in Australia just 2 years ago.🍖It's no wonder that the 'Reuben' sandwich is sold 3x more than the other sandwiches. I can personally vouch for it. Filled with beef pastrami, sauerkraut, swiss cheese, cocktail dressing on rye, it is an explosion of a straightforward classy luxury for the tongue. I've been here twice, and twice I had the Reuben.🧀Christian's concept of running the deli is simplicity; comfort food, simple, not too many staff and controllable. That being said, everything displayed and served is 95% imported from Italy; from the various kinds of cheeses to the salami and bruschetta, Christian clearly does not compromise when it comes to quality.🍲We tried the pumpkin soup, goulash soup, grilled chicken meatloaf and grilled vegetable sandwich (perfect for vegetarians), and they were simply amazing. Have a look at the pictures for yourself!🍰The Burnt Cheesecake, baked by Pearl, was incredulously rich; no flour used, just cheese, eggs and sugar. This too is a must-try.I'm glad that Hudson's deli is just nearby where I stay. It's amazing food served in simplicity, something that I will go over and over again for.
Location: 103, Jalan Chan Siew Teong, Taman Tanjung Bunga, Tanjung Bungah, Penang

Author: justa passerby
Review: The tea is usually nice , it's more on the 'not too sweet' side. However sometimes I'm feeling skeptical on buying their cold drinks , if I'm lucky , I get a decently nice tea , if not , I get this very watery ,tasteless tea with too much …MoreThe tea is usually nice , it's more on the 'not too sweet' side. However sometimes I'm feeling skeptical on buying their cold drinks , if I'm lucky , I get a decently nice tea , if not , I get this very watery ,tasteless tea with too much ice included. (Also sometimes they end up giving me cold ice teas when I ordered the hot ones) , it's troublesome to ask for an exchange as I'm only ordering via delivery services.Also it seems they only allow toppings to be added for cold drinks and not the hot ones. Personally if you want a decent tea , you definitely will have to go with hot , but make do without any toppings.Overall I like the tea , but I'm a bit on the fence due to what's pointed out above.Maybe the option of having cold drinks with or without ice should be included. It's definitely not worth it when you get the overly watery and tasteless version.Personal favorite would be the hojicha series.Edit reply *to clarify regarding the 'not too sweet' opinion , I meant it in a good way. A lot of teas out there are getting overly sweet these days even at the less sugar option , so I do enjoy chatto for this reason , but sometimes it being inconsistent when it comes to the cold drink could use a little more improvement. Eg sometimes it tastes alright , at other times too watery , for instance sometimes I get more ice in the drink on different orders. If you can make it as consistant as the hot version I would gladly give it a 5 stars. A cold without ice option would be lovely , just a suggestion though.
Location: 143, Lebuh Carnarvon, Georgetown, George Town, Penang

This restored building is very classic and tucked …MoreWe recommend learning a bit about the lifestyle of the rich and famous (A tour or Peranakan Mansion) of Penang so you can fully understand what you are seeing when you enter this building. This restored building is very classic and tucked away in a quiet "courtyard" with a beautiful Kongsi. We really enjoyed the experience of walking there, feeling as though it was 1890s in George Town. Entering the home, in all its glory and artifacts, we sat down and enjoyed a delicious meal.  Coming from the land of fish tacos (San Diego, California, USA) and the former avocado capital of the world, we took a risk ordering the fish tacos and were delighted.  Having a meal at this restaurant is an experience to cherish while in Penang.  They have lots of exotic items on the menu and our only regret is we went there our last night of 18 nights in George Town. We hope to come back and enjoy more of the offerings in the future.  Definitely a 5 star experience all around.

It is in an unfortunate location not surrounded by many other restaurants which is why it’s so quiet but the interior is clean, food is good and service is friendly. As main we ordered a rice set that was really average and the pork, only protein inside was clearly cooked and reheated. A beef soup noodle, watery and with raw veggies served on the side, the beef in it was basically a minced meat patty really unsettling for the sight, looked liked dog food in stock. I personally ordered a spicy pork stew with a side of rice that I never received. After all the starters have been served and the other two mains almost been consumed the waitress informed that they run out of RICE! I mean how is it possibile? An Asian restaurant run out of white rice come on, it’s like you go in a private beach and they run out of sand xD So to do not loose more time I ordered a stir fried noodle dish and it was awful, tasted like instant noodle and it contained more raw veggies. I can’t consider it a seafood noodle simply because were not seafood inside, to be classified as seafood noodles need to contain at least three different kinds of seafoods but I barely found 3 prawns and 3 little squids. Probably not pricey but definitely was not worth at all, decadent and hidden downtown and HIDDEN it’s how is suppose to be far from customers.Highly not recommend.

Review: If you are looking for a delicious and authentic meal option while in Penang among all the other many Penang food options, give this place a try and experience authentic Hainanese food!
